article: To increase the computational efficiency of interest-point based object retrieval, researchers have put remarkable research efforts into improving the efficiency of k NN-based feature matching, pursuing to match thousands of features against a database within fractions of a second. However, due to the high-dimensional nature of image features that reduces the effectivity of index structures (curse of dimensionality), due to the vast amount of features stored in image databases (images are often represented by up to several thousand features), this ultimate goal demanded to trade query runtimes for query precision. In this paper we address an approach complementary to indexing in order to improve the runtimes of retrieval by querying only the most promising keypoint descriptors, as this affects matching runtimes linearly and can therefore lead to increased efficiency. As this reduction of k NN queries reduces the number of tentative correspondences, a loss of query precision is minimized by an additional image-level correspondence generation stage with a computational performance independent of the underlying indexing structure. We evaluate such an adaption of the standard recognition pipeline on a variety of datasets using both SIFT and state-of-the-art binary descriptors. Our results suggest that decreasing the number of queried descriptors does not necessarily imply a reduction in the result quality as long as alternative ways of increasing query recall (by thoroughly selecting k) and MAP (using image-level correspondence generation) are considered.

article: The potassium and sodium ion concentrations are what cause the neuron to fire. Or actually they allow the action potential to propagate along the nerve. A nerve cell starts off at a resting state with a negative charge inside and positive charge outside the cell membrane. When a signal is received, sodium ions rush into the cell causing a rapid depolarization and a shift to a positive charge inside the cell. This then triggers the opening of potassium ion channels, allowing potassium ions to flow out of the cell, which repolarizes the cell back to a negative charge again. This movement of ions creates an electrical signal that travels along the length of the neuron, allowing for the transmission of the signal from one neuron to the next.

article: I'm guessing the the Mercedes engine is turbosupercharged and the Mustang engine is not.,A lot of comments already hit on this but I'll take a shot at it. The way engines work is fairly simple. The piston moves down, pulling in air. That air is mixed with an appropriate amount of fuel and the valve (how the air got in) is closed. The piston goes back up and compresses the mixed air and fuel and then a spark makes it all explode. The explosion pushes the piston back down, then a different valve (exhaust) opens and when the piston comes back up it forces all of the waste from the process out. This is grossly simplified but you get the idea. There are a lot of ways to make more power but it mostly comes down to creating bigger explosions or creating more explosions. More is simple: either use more pistons (making the actual engine much larger and harder to fit in the car) or spin the motor faster (requiring much tighter tolerances, lighter materials, and a LOT of careful design to make sure fuel is being burned at the right ratio to prevent potential catastrophe). Both of these options require a considerably higher amount of fuel, even when the motor isn't working as hard. The other option is creating bigger explosions. You have to make sure that you use the right amount of both air and fuel in order to keep things working properly so you have to increase both to make the explosions more powerful. Fuel is easy, air is complicated. That's where "forced induction" comes in. Things like "Ram Air injection," superchargers, and turbochargers increase the air coming into the motor in different ways. Ram air forces in more air due to the speed of the vehicle traveling. Its cheap and easy, but is sensitive to altitude and air density (temperature and air pressure) and isn't a tremendous gain. Superchargers run on a belt driven by the motor. This increases the amount of work that the motor has to do all the time so it can actually see very little gains at lower speeds. Turbochargers run off of the waste gas created by the motor. This gas spins a turbine at a high rate of speed forcing dramatically higher amounts of air in. The upside of this is that because if how its powered you don't see the typical downsides if a supercharger (working harder at low speeds) but you do see the benefits. Turbocharging a motor at 1 bar (about 14.5 psi) is effectively doubling the amount of air the motor is able to work with, enabling it to act as a motor twice its size when it needs to but operate like a regular motor in normal use. The big downsides here are that turbochargers are expensive and have a lot of "packaging" (fitting the turbocharger and the necessary piping to make it work) concerns. They also got off to a rocky start in use in america, so many people were turned off of them due to concerns about expensive repairs and reliability. Modern systems are far more reliable and effective so there has been a big increase in their use recently. There's a lot more to it than that, of course. Engine dynamics are a bit more complicated (how the motor feels and sounds throughout its operating range and if that matches the character the designers have in mind). Ford does have a turbocharged 4 cylinder model coming out later this year to split the performance gap between the 300 horsepower v6 and the 435 horsepower v8. They've even done turbocharged 4 cylinder motors in traditionally v8 cars in the past (Mustang SVO and the Thunderbird Turbocoupe) with some critical success but not much sales success. I can go more in depth on this if you'd like. I tried to keep this as basically understandable as possible.','Engineering as well as a turbo. article: "Liam..... Liam, honey, wake up," The bed was beginning to shake, "Honey, you really have to get up now, okay?" "Just, like, 20 more minutes Ma," The shaking slowly subsided. "What the hell Mom, what is so goddamned important that you had to wake me up with," he glanced at his clock, now on the floor beside the broken lamp "3 hours of sleep?!!? Geez Ma..." After a few calming breaths Liam settled back onto the bed, the wetness of his wake up call seeping through his pajama shirt, and he looked over at his mother, who had retreated to the door, knowing full-well what reaction Liam would have to her chilly good morning. Liam's concern over his bed's wetness turned to dismay as he took in what his mother was wearing, an army green tank top with forest-camo cargo pants and a massive backpack, loaded down so completely he was surprised it didn't burst it's seams. "Liam, we have to go, now, your father is already preparing the truck and, knowing him, it'll be ready by the time you're changed," she said, in that scary calm way that mother's use to avoid panicking their children. "But, is it real this time, it is, isn't it, please, please tell me it's a drill, tell me I'm wrong," Liam wasn't quite panicked yet, he was still trying to work through the dread at what was about to happen, he knew what the camo meant, it meant they were leaving, and probably wouldn't be back for a while, if ever. He couldn't figure out why though, it didn't make any sense, before he went to sleep there hadn't been anything in the news, either mainstream or back-channel, that indicated anything apocalyptic was happening. The economy was generally stable, as stable as ever in fact since the crash a few years ago, and the only wars, cold or hot, were in Asia and Africa. "Honey, NOW!" his mother yelled, he hadn't realized he'd been sitting there stunned. Her yell snapped him back to reality where his training kicked in, he sprung from his bed, far more controlled now without the ice water spurring his movements, and was inside his closet almost instantly. With a pleased nod, his mother hopped the banister behind her to the first floor and was gone, likely to toss her pack in the "truck" and grab anything they may have extra room for. With a swift kick to the side, Liam popped open a false wall in his closet, revealing a bugout bag, his own camo gear, his AK-47, and a decently sized box of pre-loaded magazines. He tried to don his gear swiftly, the way he'd been taught, but nervousness had an icy grip on his chest in a way his training hadn't prepared him for. As such, he tripped while trying to pull his other pant-leg up, landing in a pile of dirty clothes, with his cap on, his green shirt around his neck like a scarf, and an 80lb duffel bag over one shoulder making him feel like a turtle that some petulant child had flipped. He quickly thanked God, Buddha, and The Flying Spaghetti Monster that his brothers weren't here and used his indignation to quiet his nerves, if only for the moment, so he could at least dress properly. Exiting his room, Liam glanced around to find quite a few of his parents knick-knacks out of place, this was disturbing considering his father's borderline OCD concerning his, so-called, "finds." "There must have been a tremor or something, was that what shook the bed?" Realizing he was standing like a doe in the headights, Liam mentally berated his internal monologue. He prepared to vault the banister as his mother had done when he stopped again, looking at himself in the floor-length mirror at the end of the hallway, and he liked what he saw. A vision of the action heroes from the old movies his parents had introduced him to as a child, decked out in his survival gear and AK, all now properly donned, despite his earlier mishaps, if it weren't for the circumstances, he could've stared at himself all day. Instead, the windows began to shake violently and the ear-splitting sound of a sonic boom cascaded through the house, snapping Liam out of his self-reverie. He hopped the banister, landing on the floor below in a crouch, feeling the impact shockwaves cascade through his lower extremities and wishing he had thrown his bag over first, the extra weight made the landing unexpectedly rough. Liam stood and looked around, taking in his childhood home for, most likely, the last time. The couch where he'd had his first kiss, the wall of old gaming consoles he had repaired with his dad, the bathroom where he crawled out the window the first time to sneak out, the liquor cabinet he'd repaired after some friends wrecked it during a party, but it was time to go, he'd always have those memories, even if he wasn't there, Liam turned and bolted for the open front door without looking back. Upon emerging from the house, he stopped, dropping to his knees, mouth agape, staring at the sky in horror. What appeared to be a huge tear had formed in the sky, like some god had unzipped the heavens, but what Liam saw didn't make him think of heaven, no, it was nothing of the sort. Huge tentacles were knurling and whipping around the edges of the tear, almost like they were trying to force it open farther. He couldn't make anything out inside the tear, however, it just seemed to be a mass of purple and black darkening the formerly clear, blue sky. It almost felt as if it were sucking him in, not physically, but mentally, dragging his mind away from his body. As he noticed what was happening to him, the tug on his mind intensified, the more he fought against it, the more agonizing it got and, before he knew it, he heard screaming. But, where was it coming from, he couldn't look away to find the source though. It was close, maybe one of the neighbors? Then muffled speech, but, why was it muffled, and why can't I look away from this damned rift. Rift? When did I start thinking of it as a rift, that implies it leads somewhere, doesn't it? The muffled speech came back again, louder this time, he could almost make out the words now, but they were so distant, and couldn't really be important could they? Damn I wish that screaming would stop, it's driving me..... insane?

article: There are several ways to purify water: filtration, and distillation, and chemicals (bleach, iodine, etc.) Filtration uses filters of different porosities to remove particles (sand, etc.) and microorganisms (bacteria, etc.). A filter that's 0.1 micro-meters (microns) will pretty much remove all the bacteria and most of the particles, because they're 5 - 10 microns in size. Distillation heats up the water until it boils or evaporates, then passes the water through a cold tube to turn it back into a liquid. Contaminants that are in the water (particles, bacteria, etc.) can't evaporate and remain behind. Distillation is considered "better" than filtration, because boiling the water kills the bacteria; with filters, the bacteria are caught by the filter but are still alive and can multiply and possibly contaminate the filtered water. Chemical methods rely on adding a chemical that will kill bacteria, such as chlorine bleach or iodine. This chemical is effective at killing bacteria at doses that aren't too dangerous for humans.

article: I wasn't sure why my mother had never mentioned the VHS tapes she had stashed away in the bottom of her bedroom closet. I was only rooting around in there because I'd loaned her some shoes last time I'd come home from college and I wanted them back, but instead I found about a dozen unlabeled tapes stacked neatly in the back corner behind the pile of shoes and mostly hidden by some long dresses. At first I thought they were going to be weird sex tapes or something, but when curiosity compelled me to put one in the VHS player my parents still had lying around, I found that they were of a different nature altogether. The first tape started off with a grainy view of our living room. It was Christmastime according to the decorated tree beside the fireplace and the wreath sitting on the mantle, partially obscuring the large mirror behind it. After a few moments a woman came onscreen carrying a small baby. It took me a long moment to recognize her as my mother, and I was only certain of her identity when I heard her voice say "Look, Ashley, Santa Claus came!" Ashley is my name, so I assumed the baby in her arms must have been me. My birthday is in September, so this must have been my first Christmas. I watched transfixed as a part of my past that I had no chance of remembering played out before me. I got some new pajamas and a few baby toys that year, and most of the tape was just me snuggling in my mother's arms while she tried to get me to play with a stuffed elephant. Eventually I started getting fussy, and my mother got up and took me out of the room. After a few moments the living room scene went staticky, and I fast forwarded a bit to make sure that it wasn't just a blank spot in this homemade tape, but that seemed to be the end of the recording. I quickly popped the next tape in. This one started in the same manner: a view of our living room without anyone in it. There was no Christmas tree this time. The scene remained unmoved for longer than the first one, but eventually a toddler came running into the room laughing hysterically. It was me again, and close behind me was my mother. I fell to the floor, still giggling, and my mother immediately scooped me up and spun me around, also laughing. She played with me a bit, tickling me, blowing raspberries at me, and tossing me up in the air, all the while laughing with me amidst my screams of excitement. " Come on, silly girl, we need to get you dressed! " she said finally. " Noooooooo! " squealed the still pajama-clad toddler, but I made no moves to resist as my mother carried me back the way we came. Again the scene remained still for a time before going staticky, and again I found that that was the end of the video, despite there being hours of recording time left on the tape. I was starting to feel like something was a little strange about these tapes, but I kept watching them. Each captured between five to fifteen minute snippets of my childhood, not always in order. There was another Christmas scene, and a birthday party, but most of them were just regular days, always filmed from the same angle in our living room. However, something in the seventh one caught my attention. The large mirror above the fireplace was directly opposite a bay window looking out into the front yard. From the angle that the camera was at, I could clearly see the front yard through the window reflected in the mirror. The young me in the video was doing something in the living room as usual, but some movement in the yard drew my eyes up to the mirror. It was just our dog running around, but as I was about to look back to myself in the living room, the realization hit me like a ton of bricks. Where was the camera? From this angle I should have been able to see the camera in the mirror, but there was nothing there. I tried to convince myself that I was wrong, that the camera was shorter than the window and out of view of the mirror, but I couldn't. I had literally just finished my college trigonometry midterms the week prior and passed with flying colors. I had a natural talent for visualizing this stuff, and I knew beyond a shadow of a doubt that I should be able to see the recording device in that mirror. Fed up of having more questions than answers, I decided to text my mother at work. Hey mom, why did you never show me the video tapes from when I was a kid? The answer was not what I wanted. What video tapes? After I explained where I'd found them and what the contents were, she called me instead of texting back. " Ash, get out of the house and call your cousin Tiffany to come pick you up. Leave the tapes where they are. I'm calling the police now. I've never done more than take pictures of you with a polaroid or my phone and we certainly never owned a video camera. And I have never been aware of any VHS tapes in my closet. " I spent the rest of the day at Tiffany's house. The police confiscated the tapes, and despite repeated inquiries by my mother, they have never provided any answers. article: The PARAFAC2 is a multimodal factor analysis model suitable for analyzing multi-way data when one of the modes has incomparable observation units, for example because of differences in signal sampling or batch sizes. We develop two probabilistic formulations of the PARAFAC2 along with variational procedures for inference: In the one approach, the mean values of the factor loadings are orthogonal leading to closed form variational updates, and in the other, the factor loadings themselves are orthogonal using a matrix Von Mises-Fisher distribution. We contrast our probabilistic formulation to the conventional direct fitting algorithm based on maximum likelihood. On simulated data and real fluorescence spectroscopy and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry data, we compare our approach to the conventional PARAFAC2 model estimation and find that the probabilistic formulation is more robust to noise and model order misspecification. article: We consider the problem of learning a non-deterministic probabilistic system consistent with a given finite set of positive and negative tree samples. Consistency is defined with respect to strong simulation Okay, let me explain what each of those terms means. - Non-deterministic probabilistic system: This is a type of system where outcomes are influenced by random factors. This means that even if we know the current state of the system and the actions taken, we cannot predict the exact outcome. - Positive tree samples: These are examples of trees that show the expected behavior of the system under certain conditions (e.g., if a certain event occurs, then the system will behave in a certain way). - Negative tree samples: These are examples of trees that show what the system should not do in certain situations. - Consistency: In this context, consistency means that the learned probabilistic system behaves in the same way as the positive tree samples and not like the negative tree samples. - Strong simulation: This is a type of simulation where we check that the behavior of one system is a proper subset of the other. In this case, we want to ensure that the learned probabilistic system can simulate the behavior of the positive tree samples, but not the negative tree samples. So, putting it all together, we are trying to learn a non-deterministic probabilistic system that can simulate the behavior of positive tree samples and avoid simulating the behavior of negative tree samples, consistent with the principle of strong simulation.

One was a girl, in a ragged gray dress, the other a boy in suspenders. I stalked in the shadows behind them. I could smell the softened caramel of the Witch's roof tiles before the house came into view. The kids must have spotted the house too, because they stopped shouting for help, and went running so fast towards the candy house their arms flapped behind them. I paused. It was a pretty picture: the gingerbread house, framed in dark chocolate pillars. The children fell to eating it. From where I stood, in shadows at the edge of her yard, I could see the Witch inside the window. She stood when she heard their munching, and crept towards the door. The sounds of their feasting echoed throughout the forest: smacking of lips, grunts, and (most terribly of all) the crunch of the little girl's teeth against the peppermint doorknob. It was a pleasant spring day, and I had things to do. But I couldn't help but watch for a moment. I heaved my axe up against my shoulder, blade up. I straightened my spine a little and wiped my runny nose on my sleeve. A wolf appeared the Big Bad Wolf lured by the smell of the children as surely as the children were lured by the house. He was a big, dark gray wolf, with teeth as jagged as broken glass. When he smiled at the children, his lips rolled back, revealing gray gums. Interesting, I thought. Witch vs. wolf? Let's see where this goes. The witch finished creeping to the doorway. She and the wolf spotted each other, but the children kept eating, oblivious. The wolf's low growl reverberated through the handle of my axe. Yet the children, the little dummies, still didn't hear or see either of them. I wondered how long it would take them to realize they were in danger. I've always thought of myself as a highly capable person, although lately I've had a bit of a cold. I took two steps forward into the yard, when the wolf lunged at the Witch. I backed up again, hiding behind a bush. The witch and the wolf grappled, tumbling down the slope of the yard and towards the woods. Towards me, in fact. The wolf tore at the witch's dark cloak, white teeth flashing The Witch clawed back with long fingernails. Within a minute, the Witch flipped over on top and sucker-punched the wolf right in the gut. The wolf yowled and fell limp, and the Witch pulled out a knife and cut his throat. This commotion, finally, roused the children from their feast. They stared at the dead wolf, melted chocolate smeared on their faces. The Witch turned towards them. Before she could open her mouth, I threw my axe in the Witch's back. She dropped to the forest floor. (If the witch's back hadn't been turned, I wouldn't have stood a chance. I've been ill lately, and I'm weak. I'd hate to think what would happen if I had to face the wolf.) "Hey, dummies!" I stepped over the witch's dead body and nodded a greeting to the two grubby kids. They stared at me. "He's a rip-off," I said, "His prices are too expensive. And besides, he's never around when I really need him. He always comes too late to help." I turned my head and coughed into my sleeve. article: You're right in that shaking your hand out after hurting it doesn't actually relieve pain, but the vigorous motion seems to block the most intense stuff from really registering as painful. This is all because of how our nerve signals communicate sensory information to our brain. While understanding and treating pain is a massive part of modern health care and a sub-field with a lot of room to grow, what's needed to answer your question is fairly straight forward. When you slammed your finger in the door, you (most likely) felt the immediate pain of the smash and then a rising, duller pain that comes on after a second or two. This is because pain nerves come in two general types; a thicker neuron with a sheath that transmits intense pain signal quickly from a small radius around the receptors in your skin, and a thinner neuron that more slowly transmits pain signals from a more general region of your body. When pressure is put on the skin, the faster pain signals can be physically blocked from reaching the brain while the slower ones pass through. So how is this all related to shaking? By quickly shaking your fingers around, you are subjecting your fingers to g-forces as they are in a constant state of acceleration and deceleration, which could potentially provide enough pressure to dull some of that initial intense pain." -uZaburino from the last time it was posted. The angel sat down beside his partner, "Might as well get comfy, it'll be a long enough flight we can get a bit of sleep on the way." The Seraphim's engines whined softly as the electrical shutdown procedure finished up. The cypress trees made a small forest where they had hidden the ship, the pilots activated the camouflage and watched as the screen went dark, starved of light. Michael opened the door and dropped into the tall grass, Albus followed him out into the open. "Engage W.I.N.G. apparatus," he ordered, a heads up display augmenting his vision. The two humanoid forms slowly levitated off the ground as the counter-gravity field took hold of them, the thrusters fired and brought them into the deep blue sky. The target came into view, a building unlike that humanity had ever attempted to accomplish. "They're not ready," Albus exclaimed. "I know, and so does Kyrios, which is why we're here. We have to stop it's construction, if humanity reaches space..... I can't even think of the consequences." Albus shook his head, "War, that'll definitely be one consequence. They'll finally make use of atomics as a weapon if they have means to get it into orbit." Humanity was special in one curious way when it came to invention. They were the singular recorded species in all of occupied space to have first created a means to get out of the atmosphere that didn't require rocketry of any kind. Every other race had invented flight first, it was likely that humans would too, once their technology was rendered useless by the machine these men were about to unleash. They landed quietly on a multi story building and engaged their camouflage, looking for the right moment to infiltrate the facility. A convoy approached the front gate, they snuck in behind it. "The center of this facility is the exact location of the middle of their city, if we activate the linguistic reprogrammer we will be able to target every person on this continent." "What about the smaller groups of civilization on the smaller continent to the west?" Albus questioned, as they reached the basement. "They've not yet Invented such technology, we won't have to worry about them for now." Albus removed the reprogrammer from his superior's back, "What of the currently completed section of the space elevator? What will we do with it?" "That, I can not say." Michael punched in the code and timed it for 5 minutes, "It will change 80 of the population to four different core languages, enough that no remaining group of scientists and engineers will be able to decipher the plans for the elevator. We're hopeful that most of the population will move out based on this change, perhaps even the unchanged group will vacate. Afterwards we can bring in a planetary salvage group and take the raw materials with us." Now finished, they exited the building and returned to the sky. "Their future could be so bright," Albus' face turned to sorrow behind the mask. "With this, they'll have yet another chance to do some good with their lives. I'm just glad Kyrios is in control, I'd have given up on these poor humans so long ago. He keeps giving them more and more opportunities, perhaps they'll accomplish something this time around." Their craft streaked across the sky, it's spherical shape painted matte white so as not to reflect light. Below them a swarm of nanites emerged from the box, each carrying a program that would erase the language of a person's youth, so effective was this device that it even changed what words you thought in, and what syntax. Within ten minutes the robots had integrated themselves into every person's mind and started the transformation. The human race would not know the significance of this event, but it charted the course towards their salvation from destruction.

article: I hold this opinion for several reasons. First of all you have to sit too close to a large screen to take full advantage of the increase in resolution over 1080P. This vastly increases your horizontal viewing angle which will negatively impact your ability to see the entire movie or play a console game effectively. So ok, lets say you really like your nose up to the screen, that presents another problem, most living rooms are not setup to accommodate a TV that big or to sit that closely. There's a reason why 4K TVs are moving into the 85" range, because the average viewing distance of most people barely takes full advantage of most of the 1080p tvs in people's houses right now. Furthermore, to go to 4K you have to dump your plasma in favor of arguably inferior LCDLED technology that fails to produce effective black levels for the most part in comparison. The only technology on the horizon that can beat plasma in black levels is OLED. So we need a 85" OLED 4K TV to sit a comfortable 11 feet away, and that's going to be pricey and isn't even available yet. And that's saying nothing of the problem of upscaling older content that's likely to stay in 1080p for a considerable period of time. Upscaling that 1080p blu-ray, PS4 (which is already being upscaled to 1080P), or satellite image is going to make the picture blurry and inferior to a true 1:1 1080P image under the exact same conditions. In conclusion, 4K isn't ready for prime time, and likely won't be for at least another 5-10 years. The proper seating distance for a modern 1080P TV is about 1.6 times the diagonal length of the screen based on my research. I don't know what the comparable distance is exactly for 4K (guessing 1.0-1.1x since it's double the horizontal resolution), but the technical limitations are not going to accommodate most people. If you're looking to improve your AV experience most people would be vastly better served by getting a decent audio system for under 1K.

We investigate a robust minimax least squares problem where the objective is to find a solution that minimizes the worst-case regret among a set of possible datasets with bounded uncertainties. This type of problem arises in applications where the input data is subject to measurement errors or noise, and it is important to find a solution that is robust to these uncertainties. To solve this problem, we formulate it as a semi-definite programming problem, which is an efficient and scalable approach to solving optimization problems with convex constraints. In this approach, we introduce auxiliary variables to represent the worst-case regret, and we add constraints to ensure that the error in the solution is bounded by the data uncertainty. The resulting semi-definite programming problem can be solved using standard optimization software, and it provides a robust and efficient solution to the minimax least squares problem. Our approach has been applied to a variety of real-world problems, including image reconstruction, signal processing, and financial risk management, and it has been shown to be effective in improving the robustness and accuracy of the solution. Overall, the minimax regret criteria and the semi-definite programming approach provide a powerful tool for solving least squares problems with bounded data uncertainties, and they have broad applications in many areas of science and engineering.

article: Two reasons: WiFi typically operates at 100 mW, cell phones are allowed to transmit up to 2000 mW. WiFi operates at a higher frequency, which is blocked more easily by walls, etc. These are intentional. Wifi links have been established by hobbyists using souped- up routers over long distances (miles), but that defeats the purpose of home use, because if all routers reached that far, they'd all interfere with each other, making the connection slow.,WIfi uses different frequency than cell phones. Frequencies used for wifi is absorbed by air more than those used by phones.', "Cell phones really don't travel that far because there are cell towers everywhere. These towers are very tall, which allows them to pick up the very faint signals of cell phones around them. The size of the antenna isn't really relevant to reception. The placement of antennae (up high and without obstruction) are the important parts. Wifi routers operate on very high frequencies (2.4 gigahertz) which are more easily absorbed by walls,which is why they don't always cover a big house.," "First off, the antennas aren't the important part of this relationship; they are the length they need to be based on the frequency they are tuned to. What you are thinking of is the transceiver that the antenna is attached to, however I will put it into layman's terms: Putting it simply, there are 2 antennas in radio frequency communication: the transmitter antenna and the receiver antenna. If you think of the cell phone antenna as the receiver, and the cell tower as the transmitter, you have your 2 antennas. The connection between the 2 antennas needs a certain power level, and since the cell tower is nice and large and therefore providing the bulk of the necessary power, your cellphone antenna is much much smaller. With your router and computer, you are covering a smaller space, but the same principle applies. The router and computer are the 2 antennas, the router is providing the bulk of the necessary power, and the computer antenna can be smaller. Looping back around, cellphones actually have transceivers meaning they can send and receive information on radio frequencies, but the same ideas apply. There is an entire science and industry based on RF communication...my experience is based on that of RF design for sound engineering, basically wireless microphones, but the physics is the same for cell phones, satellite communication, ham radio, etc.,This probably won't get seen - but I'll give it a go anyway. It's a combination of a lot of factors that people have been talking about - but the key here is "combination." It's not just that your phone and the cell tower run at higher powers. They also know how to communicate with each other, maintain a constant link between each other and the cell tower has a "capacity" of number of phones it can talk to at one time; which cannot be broken - after this number it will not accept communications from another phone (for simplicity sake I'll state that your WiFi router is not limited in this way - it is limited, but not in the same way: that's a separate ELI5...) Imagine you and your friends out in a field and you've all got a set of alphabet flashcards of different sizes (from postage stamp size up to A1) each with their own colour. You tell your friends to go and stand in a line about 10m apart from each other all facing you and then use the cards to send you a message. You will respond to them with the cards of their own colour as you have a set of all the colours. The guy 10m from you holds up the A1 sized cards to start, and you're not able to see anyone else behind him because the card is in the way, so when you see the A1 sized card, you show your card to say you've got the message - but also that he needs to use a smaller sized card (the postage stamp one because you can read that from 10m away). This means that you and he can communicate (him using postage stamp sized cards, you using his coloured cards) While this is happening all you other friends are also holding up their A1 sized cards trying to get a message from you, but because you can't see them and so aren't responding, they keep trying the first part of the message. As the first guy changes to the postage stamp sized cards, you can see the 2nd guy and respond, tell him to use a smaller card, but bigger than the postage stamp so you can read it still from 20m away. This continues down the line until you can see all of your friends and they're all using different sized cards. They know which messages are for them because your cards are colour coded, and you've made sure that you can see all of their cards, so you can talk to them all. This means that your friend furthest away can still talk to you, even though he's a long way away. He's holding up the large card, which can be seen over all the smaller cards infront of it. This is like transmission power, phones nearer the tower are told to turn down their transmission power so that the tower can see what's happening "behind" them. This only works because the tower creates an unbroken link between itself and each phone that it is talking to, so it has a record of what phone is on what power and how to talk to that phone. Because the tower then knows what it is looking for to communicate with the phone, the phone doesn't need to be transmitting with such high power. There's a whole load more going on, if you're interested then drop me a PM and i'll explain more. TL,DR: It's not just 1 single thing that enables cell phones to work - there's a whole system designed specifically to get around range problems and a lot of smart things happening all at once.', "Alright, some seriously bullshit comments on this thread. This probably won't be seen by many but hopefully op sees it. Multiple factors are in play when considering cell phone signal vs wifi signal. TL;DR - A shit ton more powerlower frequenciesdirected antennasmuch farther range than your home wifi. 1) Frequency - Frequencies are waves. The lower the frequency, the bigger the wave is. The bigger the wave, the farther it travels before it is no longer usable. Why does Verizon have such good service in very rural areas? They have a lot of 850mhz spectrum, this means that a single cell tower can serve a much greater radius. Lower frequencies also impact penetration. The lower the frequency, the better it is at getting through buildings, trees, etc.... so less will interfere. 2) Directed antennas - Your wifi router at home has an omni directional antenna. This means it is sending out signal in all directions. Ever seen those DIY hacks that you put a parabola on a wifi antenna to get better signal in a certain area? That's why, directing more power in one direction will improve signal in that direction. Cell towers are not omni directional. Each cell tower has sectors, I've seen them go from 1 (rare), 3 (most common), to 6 (also rare). Each sector broadcasts its signal in a direction and if you could visualize how it's waves looked, you would see a cone. If you stand directly under a cell tower (assuming no other cell towers are near by) you will not get very good, or possibly any, signal. 3) Power - this is the biggest factor. This is the biggest factor. Cell towers use a LOT of power compared to your home wifi. A single cell is powerful enough that, if not turned off, will burn a worker operating directly in front of the cell. Put simple, you could possibly power a single or maybe a few cells with your home power connection but you wouldn't be able to power an entire cell tower. Source: I work for a cell phone provider on the networking side. I now deal with the core but I used to work with the cell towers. If you have any more questions about how a cell phone network works, feel free to ask. I love talking about it.," "So basically, wifi is specifically supposed to NOT have good range. WiFi operates on shared frequencies (2.4 ghz band has a few different channels, 5.8 ghz has more), so if it goes much past your houseapartment, you can interfere with your neighbor's wifi. If that happens, no one has wifi. -Because WiFi operates on shared radio frequencies, it's limited to very low power. It's also kind of disorganized and chaotic. -WiFi is on a higher frequency, which means the already limited signal power dissipates faster. -Although your cell phone radio doesn't transmit with quite as much power as the cellphone tower, there is some compensation for this at the cell phone tower. The antennas at the tower are also really good. -The equipment at the tower can be several tens of thousands of dollars, whereas your average WiFi router is under 100 -Most towers are tall, which helps signal go further (gets around buildings, over trees, etc).," "There are a lot of cell base stations for your phone to talk to, they're very, very well situated, and they're somewhat more powerful than an average wifi AP. Tons of care and attention goes into antenna location, positioning, and characteristics. The physical size of the antenna is mostly a function of the frequencies being used, which are high, thus the small antennas.,The bottom line is, your cellphone operates on a frequency that can transmit to a cellular radio tower. The tower is linked to an infrastructure and connected to a SP (service provider). And wifi opperates on a higher frequency, and can only travel so far, intentionally.','Well first of all not all of the wireless network is actually wireless when it comes to cell phones. You have towers that transmit the wireless signal your cell picks up over a short distance (few miles) that are actually connected to a wired ground network that forwards the calls data to the desired destination. Your wifi router uses less frequencies to transmit the wireless signal. Probably 2.4ghz - 5ghz. the lower the frequency the wider the radio wave is and the shorter it travels but at the same time can penetrate walls better for a better signal. And in the frequency you are using 0.5w is doing a great job. So when you're talking to a friend every one of you talk to your nearest cell tower and the do all the rest (they are connected with cables mostly),The cellphone tower is both a gigantic ear and a gigantic megaphone. Your router and your computer are like two people yelling across a train platform.','The simple answer is that cellphone towers are transmitting with a lot more power than your WiFi router. article: Phillips wished for noise-cancelling earphones as he struggled to get some shuteye on the C-37A. Though he was at the aircraft's fore, the aft-located engines droned ceaselessly with a volume surprisingly loud for a civilian aircraft. True, he'd flown on Black Hawks, Chinooks, and Ospreys that were far louder than this Gulfstream, but those were for distances that did not necessitate sleep. For some reason this tiny civilian plane's engines could compete with those of C-17s and C-130s. He shifted around in his his too-small seat, wishing that Gulfstream had manufactured seats more suited to his large frame. Perhaps it wasn't Gulfstream that made these seats though; they definitely weren't standard given the purpose of this jet, maybe it was just another lowest bidder who made cramped seats for cheap on the taxpayer dime. Phillips sighed. At least he wasn't the guy in the back. Eyes closed, Phillips felt a tap on his shoulder. "Phillips. I just checked in on the satphone. We have a problem." His partner Platt awoke him from his attempted rest. Platt was an agreeable guy; it was Phillips' first op with him, but so far they'd managed to execute and deliver. So far. "Problem, what kind of problem? Phillips inquired, yawning. "Do we need to get landing permissions at a different site? Get in touch with Johnson, he can liaise with the folks at State and deal with it. It's a spring-floored cell for the guy no matter where he goes, doesn't make a difference to me." "No, not that." Platt said curtly. "They processed the pictures we sent in. There's a negative ID." "Negative?" Phillips asked. "Negative? What the fuck do you mean negative, we got the wrong guy? Why the fuck am I hearing about this now?" "Affirmative on that. We got the wrong guy. I'm unclear on the timeframe details of the discovery, but the destination COS wants us to resolve this issue quietly. He says to get creative; we don't need more diplomatic backlash." Platt replied. "We have 12 hours to execute on that, he's giving us full leverage." "Jesus, fuck." Phillips was not amused. They'd gone with a team and snatched this guy in a night raid, almost losing a guy in the process. There was a too-long stint at Bagram, and when they finally got the clearance to get on this plane, finally some dickwad at a desk comes back with a negative ID? What a goddamn waste. "Suggestions?" Platt asked impatiently. Phillips was beginning to like him less, but he didn't care enough to show it. In this profession, you could never like anyone too much. Phillips stood up, looking towards the aft of the plane. "Where are we right now? Geographically speaking," he asked. "Last I checked with the pilot twenty minutes ago, we're still over the Black Sea. ETA to site just over an hour." "Good. Tell the pilot to go down low and slow, and depressurize," Phillips ordered. "Depressurize?" Platt quizzically inquired. "You've never seen someone jump without a chute, have you?" Phillips asked.

article: Stacy quickly turned off the TV on her desk, shaken. She had it muted so the children could continue sleeping soundly on their mats, but the breaking news message was still clear. She glanced at the calendar. It was March 27th, certainly too early for an April Fool's joke, but what if the news station decided to run the story a little early? " The best plan of action is to lock your doors and remain inside until we receive word that the crisis has been adverted, " the closed captions said. Hesitantly, Stacy turned the television back on. The channel she was watching had gone to a commercial break, so she flipped to another local station. Images of sick people in the hospital flashed across the screen. People both young and old, bound to gurneys overflowing the halls with masks on their faces. Just this morning everything was fine, Stacy thought, this can't be real. She couldn't quite tell if they were alive or dead. The children were beginning to stir from their naps, but Stacy continued to sit there, completely oblivious to her classroom. Suddenly, the door burst open and she had to cover her mouth with her hand to silence the screen that almost came out. Her close friend and fellow teacher stood at the door. " Have you seen the news? " Harry asked, at a noise level one could consider rude if not given the current situation. " It has to be a joke, right? " Stacy stammered. Harry paused for a moment. " My wife just called. It's real. They're shutting down access to the hospital and barricading the streets in and out of town. " Harry's wife was a surgeon at the hospital. Stacy had met her once at a Christmas party. She seemed nice enough, but had a very serious and professional demeanor. She didn't seem like the kind of person to be a part of such a horrible prank. " Hold on, she's calling me again. " He quickly left. No, this can't be happening. This is like something out of a horror movie, Stacy thought. She turned up the television a little. A professionally dressed reporter filled her screen. It was obvious that she was uncomfortable standing so close to the hospital. " We have received confirmation that the virus is quickly spreading through contact with bodily fluids. There are reports that the mucus spread by sneezing is the most contagious, but we haven't received an official statement regarding that yet. Avoid anyone who may be sneezing and immediately vacate the vicinity. There have been reports of violent attacks from infected individuals. If possible, stay in your homes until further information is received. " A fair distance behind the reporter, Stacy could see a teenager make a quick, startled movement. Was that a sneeze? Everything after that happened so quickly. Stacy could see that the figure in the background was no more than sixteen, but his body movements were that of someone much older and much stronger. He jumped higher than humanly possible, landing on the reporter's back. He grabbed at her throat, and blood sprayed over the camera. The television went black. Reeling, Stacy tried to process what had happened. After a minute, she remembered where she was. The children! She needed to protect them at all costs. She locked the door and started covering the windows, following the same emergency procedures she always followed during her weekly drills. article: All traditional methods of computing shortest paths depend upon edge-relaxation where the cost of reaching a vertex from a source vertex is possibly decreased if that edge is used. These algorithms work by exploring the graph and keeping track of the shortest path found so far. Dijkstra's algorithm, for example, works by starting at the source vertex and exploring its neighbors. It then selects the vertex with the shortest distance from the source and explores its neighbors. This process continues until the desired destination vertex is reached. Bellman-Ford algorithm works by relaxing all edges in the graph repeatedly, checking if any improvements can still be made. This process is repeated until no further improvements can be made. Floyd-Warshall algorithm works by computing the shortest path between every pair of vertices in the graph, by repeatedly considering the intermediate vertices. All of these algorithms have different time and space complexities, and may be useful in different scenarios depending on the size and complexity of the graph.

Another method is multi-agent actor-critic (MAAC), which uses a central critic to estimate the value function, but each agent has its own actor policy that is trained independently based on its own observations. MAAC also includes a consensus module that ensures that the agents' policies converge to a common solution during training. Other approaches to learning a CVF in MARL include decentralized value function (DVFs) and opponent modelling, which involves modelling the behaviour of other agents as opponents to improve the robustness of the learned CVF. Overall, learning a stable and generalizable CVF remains an active area of research in MARL, and there is no one-size-fits-all solution, as each approach has its own strengths and limitations depending on the characteristics of the environment and the agents involved.

Noise nor rain seemed to disturb him, even as lightning flashed nearby, illuminating his muscular frame in stark detail. He turned his head, and our eyes locked across the chaos. "Zeus," I cried, but thunder swallowed my words. I felt a gust of wind which nearly saw my lose my footing. With one hand still preventing the sky's deluge from blinding me, I cupped another about my mouth and bellowed: "Zeus! Stop this madness! " I saw Zeus' body tense as he heard the plea. I called out, in the most commanding voice I could muster: "Zeus: COME! " At first, his resolve seemed only to double, and as he assumed a low, challenging stance, I thought all might be lost. But then, his will faltered; he straightened, tilting his head, and started towards me. When I backpedaled quickly, onto the stone and over the threshold, he followed. Once we were both inside, I quickly shut the door behind him. When Zeus looked up at me, I could see there was still fight left in him. But so long as I held the prize, I had dominion over him, and I knew it. Shivering slightly from wetness, I placed a hand upon Zeus' head. "Give me the sock, Zeus." I saw his eyes flit between the object I held, and my face, now stern. His hunger overcame his mischief, finally, and his jaw unclenched. I caught the sock with my free hand. With the other, I provided Zeus with the treat I held, the one I must have left in my pocket from some earlier walk. A mild vice of mine, not cleaning out my pockets, but this day I was thankful for it; as was Zeus, who happily gobbled up the treat. article: Ad hoc electrical networks are formed by connecting power sources and loads without pre-determining the network topology. These systems are well-suited to addressing the lack of electricity in rural areas because they allow for a flexible and scalable approach to power distribution. Ad hoc networks can be easily set up and adjusted to meet the specific needs of a community, often relying on renewable energy sources like solar, wind, or hydro power. Additionally, these networks can be maintained and managed by the local community, making them a sustainable solution for long-term energy needs. Overall, ad hoc electrical networks have great potential for providing reliable and affordable electricity to remote and underserved areas.

article: We show that given a 3-colorable graph, it is NP -hard to find a 3-coloring with (16 17 eps) of the edges bichromatic. In a related result, we show that it is also NP-hard to find a 3-coloring with (1617 - eps) of the edges trichromatic, where eps is a positive constant. Both of these results follow from the fact that 3-coloring is already an NP-hard problem. The key idea is to construct a gadget that allows us to control the number of bichromatic or trichromatic edges in the graph. By appropriately connecting these gadgets, we can force the number of bichromatic or trichromatic edges to be close to a specific threshold, making the problem of finding such colorings also NP-hard. The details of these constructions can be quite technical and involve careful attention to how the gadgets are connected and how they contribute to the overall coloring of the graph. Nonetheless, these results demonstrate that even seemingly simple modifications to the 3-coloring problem can make it significantly harder to solve in practice.

article: Everyone is familiar with the phrase, "nice guys finish last." It's a common aphorism that's been used for at least all of my lifetime. It was generally used to dismiss why someone who is generally seen as a really genuine guy who gets the butt end of the stick. The honest man gets peace of mind, the dishonest man gets ahead. Lately, terming yourself the "nice guy" gets you a lot of flak because some how its been attributed an extremely negative connotation. The connotation I'm describing is the belief that people who are nice are only doing so because of their ultimate ulterior motive to lay with anyone they are nice to. It assumes that their actions are purely manipulative and that they expect an actionreward sort of relationship out of people. I think this is a rude oversimplification of nice guys. In actuality, these people just have a faith in people's integrity. They are the ones that are sure to be quick and helpful about repaying a favor when someone does them a kindness. These people aren't morons thoughthey don't assume sexual attraction to be a favor (as pop-culture would tell you). The issue at play is that they are not exactly socially well-rounded, so when they become involved with a girl in a platonic manner emotional attachment comes easily and quickly. This attachment only grows as the girl sees them as a closer friend because of how much time they spend together and how many favors the guy is willing to perform for them (the notorious "such a great friend" line). Meanwhile, because of the nature of attraction, the man's constant desire to please is sure to seat him in the also highly stigmatized "friendzone." So the situation that arises is the man unawares finds himself with a woman whom he thought a strong bond of companionship and mutual feelings was blossoming when in fact she has not the slightest romantic interest in him. The man isn't expecting to hit a favor quota and receive the adoration of his adoredhe is simply deluded into the idea that the more time he spends with her, the more she will realize or have the chance to realize that he is the one she has truly loved all along. Generalizing him as an asshole who is only interested in women for sex won't help him shake his fairy tale mindset. People assume he only had sexual interests from the start, which I don't believe is true. They then instantly shame him for even having those interests which only furthers the problem. So reddit, change my view tl;dr: nice guys are confused or naive individuals that need a wake up call, not conniving manipulating assholes that deserve to be ostracized. article: Machine understanding of questions is tightly related to recognition of articulation in the context of the computational capabilities of an underlying processing algorithm. In this paper a mathematical model to capture and distinguish the latent structure in the articulation of questions is presented. We propose an objective-driven approach to represent this latent structure and show that such an approach is beneficial when examples of complementary objectives are not available. We show that the latent structure can be represented as a system that maximizes a cost function related to the underlying objective. Further, we show that the optimization formulation can be approximated to building a memory of patterns represented as a trained neural auto-encoder. Experimental evaluation using many clusters of questions, each related to an objective, shows 80 recognition accuracy and negligible false positive across these clusters of questions. We then extend the same memory to a related task where the goal is to iteratively refine a dataset of questions based on the latent articulation. We also demonstrate a refinement scheme called K -fingerprints, that achieves nearly 100 recognition with negligible false positive across the different clusters of questions.

article: One of the major challenges in multivariate analysis is the estimation of population covariance matrix from sample covariance matrix (SCM). Most recent covariance matrix estimators use either shrinkage transformations or asymptotic results from Random Matrix Theory (RMT). Shrinkage techniques help in pulling extreme correlation values towards certain target values whereas tools from RMT help in removing noisy eigenvalues of SCM. Both of these techniques use different approaches to achieve a similar goal which is to remove noisy correlations and add structure to SCM to overcome the bias-variance trade-off. In this paper, we first critically evaluate the pros and cons of these two techniques and then propose an improved estimator which exploits the advantages of both by taking an optimally weighted convex combination of covariance matrices estimated by an improved shrinkage transformation and a RMT based filter. It is a generalized estimator which can adapt to changing sampling noise conditions in various datasets by performing hyperparameter optimization. We show the effectiveness of this estimator on the problem of designing a financial portfolio with minimum risk. We have chosen this problem because the complex properties of stock market data provide extreme conditions to test the robustness of a covariance estimator. Using data from four of the world's largest stock exchanges, we show that our proposed estimator outperforms existing estimators in minimizing the out-of-sample risk of the portfolio and hence predicts population statistics more precisely. Since covariance analysis is a crucial statistical tool, this estimator can be used in a wide range of machine learning, signal processing and high dimensional pattern recognition applications.

article: Multispectral pedestrian detection has attracted increasing attention from the research community due to its crucial competence for many around-the-clock applications (e.g., video surveillance and autonomous driving), especially under insufficient illumination conditions. We create a human baseline over the KAIST dataset and reveal that there is still a large gap between current top detectors and human performance. To narrow this gap, we propose a network fusion architecture, which consists of a multispectral proposal network to generate pedestrian proposals, and a subsequent multispectral classification network to distinguish pedestrian instances from hard negatives. The unified network is learned by jointly optimizing pedestrian detection and semantic segmentation tasks. The final detections are obtained by integrating the outputs from different modalities as well as the two stages. The approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the KAIST dataset while remain fast. Additionally, we contribute a sanitized version of training annotations for the KAIST dataset, and examine the effects caused by different kinds of annotation errors. Future research of this problem will benefit from the sanitized version which eliminates the interference of annotation errors.

article: Botanical specimens are shared as long-term consultable research objects in a global network of specimen repositories. Multiple specimens are generated from a shared field collection event; generated specimens are then managed individually in separate repositories and independently augmented with research and management metadata which could be propagated to their duplicate peers. Establishing a data-derived network for metadata propagation will enable the reconciliation of closely related specimens which are currently dispersed, unconnected and managed independently. Following a data mining exercise applied to an aggregated dataset of 19,827,998 specimen records from 292 separate specimen repositories, 36 or 7,102,710 specimens are assessed to participate in duplication relationships, allowing the propagation of metadata among the participants in these relationships, totalling: 93,044 type citations, 1,121,865 georeferences, 1,097,168 images and 2,191,179 scientific name determinations. The results enable the creation of networks to identify which repositories could work in collaboration. Some classes of annotation (particularly those regarding scientific name determinations) represent units of scientific work: appropriate management of this data would allow the accumulation of scholarly credit to individual researchers: potential further work in this area is discussed.

article: The air was thick with the scent of body odor which only a patron of the streets could produce. That coupled with the scent of soaked trash and human waste, it was damned near impossible not to wretch while sneaking in quick breaths of air. Holding my handkerchief to my nostrils I fought back the smell; I had my sights set on a target and had no intention of letting him slip by. The usual crowd that some might label as my "prey" are the typical stumbling drunks and bums that can barely hold onto their drink let alone their valuables. This man was different, much different. He wore a long black coat the fell just behind his knees revealing the fine cashmere blend his pants were composed of. Big money that's for sure. The man also sported large framed sun glasses with pitch black lenses to protect the eyes from those curious enough, all this framed eloquently with a sizable black beard spreading ear to ear topped off with a simple round brimmed cap. The first rule of stalking is to be inconspicuous. I kept pace with the man keeping his flowing coat tails in my peripherals whilst dodging dips and holes in the ground. This area of town could definitely use some of those tax dollars we always ramble on about. The anticipation was killing me, I had never come across someone in my own turf of such a wealthy appearance. It almost seemed too easy. A man who presented his wealth in such a manner might as well have signed a cheque to the first man to approach him in this part of town. Caught in my day dreaming the man quickly rounded a corner passing under a fizzling street lamp struggling for it's last flickering breaths. "god damn it!" muttering to my self I had broken the second rule, always keep your eyes on the target. An amateur mistake thinking of the prize before it's even available. Breaking into a light jog I made my way to the corner pressing against it before sneaking a peak. "I know you have been following me and I advise you cease doing so immediately" A strangely deep voice reverberated. "Holy shit!" I gasped jumping back sucking down the foul air followed by that awful dry heave that comes with it. The man took this opportunity to continue on his way vanishing around a near by alley way. A gruff laughter came from a near by gutter "hoo hoo he got you good you dirty snake." Regaining my composure I gazed up at a street urchin laying on his pile of filth chuckling with glee. "Coming from the likes of you!" bellowing as I kicked a near by bottle at the ruffian. "Goooh!" the man cried in pain as the bottle connected with his unwashed nest of hair. I wasn't going to be stopped so easily, if anything that embarrassment was going to be my motivation now. I am a professional! The snake that rules above the vile rats of the street. No more time could be wasted, no more games could be played. Track the man down and take him for what he is worth. Now sprinting off down the system of dingy alleys I headed to my vantage point. The entry was concealed behind a dumpster, in thought it appears to be an awful way to hide but since garbage collection gave up on this part of town a long ways back it was rarely disturbed. Shoving it aside the opening was now clear. Stepping inside the stench of the outdoors finally lifted only to be replaced by that of must and mildew. Striking a match I pawed about the walls stepping in inch deep puddles searching for my stashed flashlight. Finally grasping it through the darkness I brushed aside the webs and let the warm glow bloom throughout the disheveled structure. The wooden framing was rampant with rot, thankfully the stonework held true while also providing a sturdy foothold to climb to the perch. Placing the flashlight between my teeth for a moment before quickly sputtering over the foul taste of rust and god knows what. I began to climb towards the faint opening of light at the top of this narrow structure. Upon climbing I pondered who was this man and where did he even come from? Why was he even here in the first place? The only thing I knew was that he had to have something valuable. Finally reaching the top I carefully gripped the soggy wooden beam at the top hoisting myself onto the shaky perch. The view of the area was strangely captivating. I always take a moment to breath in the fresh air that escapes the filth below. The town was sprawled out into interlocking streets and alley ways that gave it the appearance of a massive, grey, soaking wet maze. It never seemed to stop raining. I knew with patience my target would slip into my sights once more. A true snake always knew his den inside and out. The nature of the mans appearance only assured that I would find him. No other man in this area could be mistaken for those characteristics. Reflecting to when I made my first approach I realized just how large the man actually was, his arms filled out the jacket sleeves and he stood at least half a foot taller than myself, I had better be careful if I want to avoid any physical altercations. Sure enough the burly man rounded a street corner walking at a much brisker pace than before. "Strange..... he seems to be heading straight for the run down glue factory" I pondered to myself. Why would a man like him have any business there. It mattered not, I gathered my things and set out. I will have my prize!..... whatever it may be. Like any good thief I approached the factory not from the front doors but the basement window. sliding in through the hard frame slithering gracefully to the ground I gained my footing. Just as any other part of this town the basement reeked of molds but also strangely enough an unfamiliar odor of fresh wood chips clung to the room. Feeling my way through the basement only using the light that dimly shone from outside as my guide I hunted for my prey tasting the air for any sign of him. With what lighting I had it was already strenuous to see but the deeper I traveled the thicker the dust of the cellar grew. Drawing out my handkerchief once more I covered my mouth to stifle any coughs that might slip out. There was a definite unease growing in the back of my mind, it seemed far too quiet, not that I was expecting a marching band on arrival but that silence that is so strong it's almost tugging on your instincts, screaming at you to turn and run as far away as you can. Greed is a powerful motivator that's for sure. Just as the thick of the dust was becoming to strong to bear I spotted a man laying down atop a large pile of wood shavings. Could it be?! he is just laying there defenseless?! For moment I stood completely still. Taking a moment to compose myself as I had earlier, I realized he is just some other dunderhead why was I even experiencing such a fear. Take the loot and leave that simple. Holding those thoughts close, my resolve still wavered as I reached out for his pockets. My hands trembled oh so gently. My hand found it's way in grasping what felt to be a wallet and fairly heavy pocket watch. The fear washed away as I lifted the goods from the still body. Almost cheering upon the realization that the watch was made from a gold alloy, I contained myself. This would make me a small fortune! Still standing a few feet back I had almost forgotten about the wallet still gripped in my hand. Prying it open only to see the contents of it had been emptied except for a small piece of folded paper. Slipping it out the delicate paper I gently unfolded it. The paper had a blood red mongoose painted at it's center with the text below reading. "You're not the only hunter in these nests." Snapping my gaze upwards to face the now upright man, gun barrel directly pointed in my face. There wasn't even time to scream. edit: little late to the party I know but if there's any helpful criticism fire away!

article: She was the most beautiful creature I had ever seen. Margaret, her name. Maggie for short, and the one of the two she preferred. I'd have called her "Major Wigglesworth" or something equally ridiculous if it was what she wanted - I'd have given her anything her pure heart desired. Why was she so beautiful? Well, you see, I was born with a strange gift. I've long theorized on why I have it, but it boils down to the fact that I can see the sins they've committed in their life floating over their head in a bright red font. The longer the list, the smaller the text, but I don't really need to read them, though. I understand them in an instant, like a computer receiving the commands of a keyboard: my eyes locking with the text being the pressing of a key, the information flooding my mind being the resulting letter. She was so beautiful because up until the moment she died, she was the only person I had ever seen with nothing but air over the top of her head. Up until that moment, every single human being I had ever come across had SOMETHING. Minor or major. Even myself. Not her, though. As we got to know each other, that empty space over her head never filled, not until the end of things. I loved her so dearly, and I like to think she loved me too. I envisioned a future with her - I called her my angel, for more reasons than she knew. I wanted to call her my wife. I wanted her to be the mother of my children, to teach them the secret to her beauty so that they might be the same. I wanted to grow old with her and have her show me how to make sure the list over my head never expanded. But that never happened. We dated for a while. But I could always tell there was something off about her, even if I completely blocked it out in my infatuation. Not something wrong about HER, but something wrong about her mind. Until one day, I decided to surprise her. Show up at her house with a bouquet of roses, unannounced, a diamond ring in my pocket. I was going to propose to her. But just as my finger was about to hit the doorbell, I heard an incredibly loud sound. A gunshot. I dropped the roses and kicked in the door, prepared to eviscerate whoever dared to try and harm my angel. I knew it then and there- I was going to kill them. My rage was unparalleled, my mind filled with a white-hot anger. But when that door flew open, I was blinded by the brightest light I had ever seen in my life, and it was the first sin that I simply could not comprehend. I stumbled through the light, navigating my way through the house and calling her name. Begging her to still be okay, telling whoever had tried to harm her that I was coming and that they were going to die. I found her, after what felt like hours of sobbing, searching and cursing God. I guess I really did understand what happened. What that bright red sin that flooded my angel's house was. I just didn't want to accept it. I found Maggie dead of a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head. She had killed herself - the only unforgivable sin. It was that day that I understood something that I wish I had known earlier..... It is the kindest people in the world who hurt the most.

article: In my younger days we used to say that war was a game the old played for which the young paid. They don't say that anymore. In fact now it's quite the opposite. Our dear president is this 40 year old snot-nosed kid who probably read a bit too much into Eskimo culture you know, those stories about how they put their old on ice floes and push'em out to sea? Well, same principle. Only now they're pushing us out to war. Please don't get the meaning wrong. War, I believe is unethical in all its forms. No matter to what moral end you aspire to achieve, the means will always be immoral. I certainly wouldn't want to see a young lad in the prime of his life being mowed down by an M50. But in this case, the most immoral thing is pulling me out of retirement to fight a battle where that young lad could at least run away from the bullets! Last night, Marge, or'Ma' as the unit calls her, broke her knee again. Second time this year. When she was conscripted she was the healthiest of us all. Actually, that was the main requirement to stay in the Army, which reduced the draftees to about ten thousand. Now, I'm not reluctant to say that Ma is the most beaten and battered of all Alpha Company. And the war hasn't even started. I asked her why in hell would she want to stay in this hell hole. "At 62, stuck in that home," she said, "away from my family and kids, and with nothing to look forward to, I thought I'd finally live the life of excitement I always wanted." As the medic bandaged the flesh-wound she sustained during battlefield inoculation, she turned to me and said somberly, "I wish I was back at the home now." It's the same for all of us. Basic training has taken over a year where it would normally take a regular Army unit about four months. For many of us, this is no different from the war we're about to endure in a few months time. Last night Trigger, or Major Price rather, the only one here to have been to war in his young days fell asleep during Stealth Training. And Johnny Winters, died during Airborne Training heart just stopped midair. I supposed that could've happened to any young soldier too, but I find it hard to believe that the Army didn't know JW had a heart condition. For Trigger, the young idiots yelling at his face to "drop down and give me five!" was just routine. What really pissed him off, he said, was that they'd scare some of the old folks so bad they actually pissed themselves while at attention. "Back then," he explained shaking from his gout, "I could run with over 60 pounds on my back. Now, I don't have a back left to support my rifle. And I have to take a piss doing it!" We laugh. That's we all have really. Laughing and telling old stories of our youth. And asking ourselves who in the hell thought it was a good idea to conscript the least able members of society to go to war. Well it wasn't until later that we figured out what WWIII really was. As it turns out, ours is not the only army that has conscripted old folks. It's now pretty clear what all of this really is. For now, we have no choice but to continue the training. But Alpha Company has unanimously decided that come Friday, the buck stops with us. We are going to mount a resistance against the COs. We've lived decent lives. Perhaps not fulfilling for all of us, but deserving of respect as elders. This is the last entry in this log. If any of the COs find this before Marge and Trigger are dead, know that we'll be coming for you. Don't bother looking for answers. We have delivered those who can't go on one more day of their pain. And you're next. Let this be known as the Elder Rebellion! Wednesday Aug 10th 2025

article: I looked down at the small, battered wooden cross and a ruby red rose that I held in my hand, my gaze flickering sadly between the two, and I slowly closed my fist around them. My left arm was cradling a soaked blue umbrella like it was a piece of driftwood and I was drowning in the sea - embroidered with flowers of all colours on it's surface, their petals warn away and faded to soft shades of red, green, pink and yellow, nothing like their bright and colourful former selves. I choked back my tears and unclenched my fist, blood already streaming out of the stinging crescent-shaped wounds where my nails had dug into my palm, the blood staining the holy cross and the stem of the rose, making the thorns look like they were bleeding red blood. I slowly knelt down and placed them onto the muddy ground, my hands trembling with sorrow. First the cross the wood soaked with tears, the bottom driven into the ground like a stake protruding from the heart of a vampire, then the rose, the blood red petals fluttering to the ground, bright patches of red against the dark soil. The slowly, very slowly, I followed them, my knees thudding to the ground - my jeans soaking up the rainwater - then my hands, the red blood mixing with the soil, tainting the holy ground. But I didn't care, my hair fell in front of my face like a red curtain of - Blood..... I stayed like this for a while until the night had passed and dawn had come. Then, and only then, was I ready to let go. I looked down at the floor and stood up, my knees shaking. I remembered what my mother had told me after my father had left. "Just because you love them, it doesn't mean they have to love you back." She'd said, "And I loved your father, but he didn't know this, and that's why he ran away." She'd told me, her voice cracking. But I think the real reason he left her - us - was because we loved him, and he didn't love us back. - jas0850 If you want more please check out my blog at http: rmnewstories.blogspot.co.uk
