article: Despite substantial progress in signal source separation, results for richly structured data continue to contain perceptible artifacts. In contrast, recent deep generative models can produce authentic samples in a variety of domains, such as images and sounds. These models learn to represent high-dimensional data in a lower-dimensional latent space, allowing for efficient sampling and manipulation. However, it can be challenging to use these models for source separation, as the latent space may not be designed to encode meaningful source information. To address this challenge, recent work has explored using adversarial training to learn a disentangled representation where different sources are separated in the latent space. This can be accomplished through the use of adversarial losses that encourage the model to generate samples that violate certain statistical independence assumptions between sources. Additionally, some approaches use auxiliary information, such as class labels or timing information, to further disentangle the sources. Overall, the use of deep generative models for source separation remains an active area of research. While current methods may not yet match the performance of more traditional signal processing techniques, these models have the potential to overcome limitations of earlier methods and improve performance on challenging source separation tasks.

article: The newly emerging wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) have recently drawn significant attention, where radio signals are used to power wireless terminals for information transmission. In this paper, we study a WPCN where one multi-antenna access point (AP) coordinates energy transfer and information transfer tofrom a set of single-antenna users. A harvest-then-transmit protocol is assumed where the AP first broadcasts wireless power to all users via energy beamforming in the downlink (DL), and then the users send their independent information to the AP simultaneously in the uplink (UL) using their harvested energy. To optimize the users' throughput and yet guarantee their rate fairness, we maximize the minimum throughput among all users by a joint design of the DL-UL time allocation, the DL energy beamforming, and the UL transmit power allocation plus receive beamforming. We solve this non-convex problem optimally by two steps. First, we fix the DL-UL time allocation and obtain the optimal DL energy beamforming, UL power allocation and receive beamforming to maximize the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of all users. This problem is shown to be in general non-convex; however, we convert it equivalently to a spectral radius minimization problem, which can be solved efficiently by applying the alternating optimization based on the non-negative matrix theory. Then, the optimal time allocation is found by a one-dimension search to maximize the minimum rate of all users. Furthermore, two suboptimal designs of lower complexity are proposed, and their throughput performance is compared against that of the optimal solution.

article: The analysis of the modular structure of networks is a major challenge in complex networks theory. The validity of the modular structure obtained is essential to confront the problem of the topology-functionality relationship. Recently, several authors have worked on the limit of resolution that different community detection algorithms have, making impossible the detection of natural modules when very different topological scales coexist in the network. Existing multiresolution methods are not the panacea for solving the problem in extreme situations, and also fail. Here, we present a new hierarchical multiresolution scheme that works even when the network decomposition is very close to the resolution limit. The idea is to split the multiresolution method for optimal subgraphs of the network, focusing the analysis on each part independently. We also propose a new algorithm to speed up the computational cost of screening the mesoscale looking for the resolution parameter that best splits every subgraph. The hierarchical algorithm is able to solve a difficult benchmark proposed in [ ] , encouraging the further analysis of hierarchical methods based on the modularity quality function.

article: A changing scope and 19th century tactics facing down 20th century realities. As originally conceived by Churchill (yes that Churchill) and his counterparts in the Navy, Gallipoli involved exactly zero ground troops. It was intended as a purely naval operation to force Turkey out of World War I and open up a new supply route to Russia. However, as the planning progressed, it became clear that the naval element would not be sufficient and that land forces would be necessary to achieve the objectives. This necessitated a major change in the scope of the operation and the deployment of troops. Unfortunately, the tactics employed by the Allied forces in Gallipoli were outdated and ill-suited to the realities of 20th-century warfare. The attack was launched with a massive frontal assault, relying on infantry charges and naval bombardment to soften up the Turkish defenses. This approach proved ineffective against the modern technologies and tactics employed by the Turkish defenders, who were able to inflict heavy casualties on the advancing Allied troops. Despite these challenges, the Allies persisted in their efforts, committing more troops and resources to the operation. However, the campaign ultimately failed to achieve its objectives, costing the lives of thousands of Allied troops and damaging the credibility of Churchill and his allies in the process. In hindsight, Gallipoli is widely regarded as a case study in the dangers of inflexible thinking and outdated tactics in the face of rapidly changing realities.

article: In this paper, we present a novel low rank representation (LRR) algorithm for data lying on the manifold of square root densities. Unlike traditional LRR methods which rely on the Euclidean distance metric between data points, our proposed method takes into account the underlying manifold structure of the data to better capture its intrinsic geometry. This is done by representing each data point as a square root density matrix, which is a positive semi-definite matrix that captures the local distribution of the data. Our method involves solving a convex optimization problem that seeks to find a low-rank approximation of the data matrix subject to a constraint that enforces the manifold structure. Specifically, we constrain the representation matrices for neighboring data points on the manifold to be similar to each other. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed LRR algorithm for square root densities. It outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency, indicating its potential for use in various applications such as image segmentation and clustering.

article: So for those who do not know, if you are diagnosed with ADHD in America, you get extra time on all assessments (including the SAT.) This allows some students to have double the time on school assessments than the normal kids (this does not happen on the SAT.) Not only do they get extra time, it is often impossible to take the extra time at the same time they sit the test, so therefore they have to come back later, allowing them to see the questions on the test and look up any answers they do not know. The real problem is that it is unfair to employers. So let's say there are two kids, Jack and Bill. Jack has extra time because of ADHD. He gets a 4.0 GPA instead of a 3.0GPA because of his extra time. Bill does not have ADHD, and gets a 3.4 GPA. Bill cannot get into as good a college as Jack. Now they graduate from college, but Jack has graduated from a better college. As an employer, it would make sense to hire Jack. Yet if Bill and Jack were given the same time to complete a task, Bill would do it better. So why give kids extra time on tests because they cannot pay attention? Being able to pay attention is an important aspect of how attractive you are to an employer, so we should not cater to them in high school just so they feel like it is "fair," even though really it makes it unfair for a kid who does not have ADHD or a kid who does not pretend to have ADHD. EDIT: I phrased the opening paragraph poorly. When I said kids often come back later to finish the test, I was referring to school tests and quizzes. Not the SAT. Due to the fact that you almost always have a class following the class you have your test in, you cannot just skip that class, therefore you have to come back at the end of the day or on a different day when you have a free. The SAT is not taken during school time, therefore they can have double the allotted time without interfering with another commitment. Thanks to uRobbicus and uthemcos for pointing this out. article: "A baby?!" Satan blinked at me incredulously. "Why in the ever loving fuck would I want a baby? What would I do with it?!" It didn't look like Satan as it sat across the cafe table from me. I thought that was how it worked, give a baby to the Devil and get something in return. Never really thought about what happens to it after. " Satan placed it's beautiful face into it's hands. " Human stupidity never ceases to amaze me. I don't want a baby, I have no use for it. " " I mean, you could eat it. Or take it's soul, that's a thing right? " Lucifer looked up from their hands with abject horror. " That's disgusting. I would never eat anything spawned from a pack of upgraded primates. Especially something of yours, you have issues. " Satan was telling me I had issues....what the fuck? I just didn't want to be a dad, I couldn't afford it, I wasn't ready, hated kids. Pick an excuse and it was one of the reasons I had arranged this coffee date with the Devil. " Look, I'm just not cut out to be a father, would mess up any kid I ever had. I mean, you even said I had issues right? " Lucifer nodded, folding their hands into a pyramid. " Cathy won't listen, I love her, but I can't be a dad. And ever since she heard she has been set on being a mom, and me being a dad, and us being a family. I don't know what to do, and it has gotten so bad that I am asking SATAN for help. So please....help me. " They sighed and closed their strange orange eyes. " She won't even consider adoption? " I shook my head. " She wants to be a mother so badly, but no matter how great a mom she is, it wouldn't ever be enough to make up for my lacking qualities. No patience, no money, no real prospects. We live with two other people that help with bills. We are in no way prepared to be parents, but Cathy won't see that. She would rather ruin a kid than be without it at this point. " " And you would rather sell it to the Devil. " It wasn't a question, obviously, that's why we were here. " Fine. I will take it. " My head snapped up to meet their eyes, blank but for my own reflection. A slow smile spread on that pretty face that displayed far too many sharp teeth. " But. " Satan said. " But? " " You must pay a price. " " Wait....But I'm giving YOU something. " This wasn't how this was supposed to go. " Yes, a burden. " they sipped their coffee. " You see, infant souls are pure and fresh. Untainted by the sins of man if you will. " They took a sip. " I have no use for servants like that, and raising one would be far too much work, I mean, dad did it and look what happened. " Another sip. " And as for the soul itself, the only thing I could really do would be to return it to the well for recycling. As it is of course, pure, and can not really be used as energy for any dark purpose. " Another sip. Sweat was beginning to trickle down my neck now. Maybe this hadn't been such a good plan. " So Mike this is really more of a favor I would be doing for you, rather than you for me. " They drained their cup and motioned to the waitress for another without even looking, knowing that within minutes the cup would be refilled. " My price, since you seem to not care much for the fate of your unborn, will be suffering inflicted upon you, contingent on the suffering of Cathy at the loss of her child. " That may be a game changer. I thought to myself and Satan smirked like they had heard me, they probably had. I mean, people move on. The loss of the baby will devastate her of course, but she will move on. You are a terrible person. You love Cathy and you are willing to hurt her because you are selfish as fuck. A wider smile from the Devil. They could definitely hear the internal conflict I was having. Yeah but she hates kids too, can't stand babies or diapers, can't stand their screaming and everything about them. SHE HATES BABIES! A chuckle, well more like a hissing laugh between dagger teeth. I would be doing us a favor. " What is the price? " " I already said, suffering equal to that of Cathy's. " I knew Cathy, ultimately she would realize that it was better that way. I would be able to bear the suffering knowing I could continue my life, comforted by the fact that my girlfriend is emotionally rational and that she would agree that we would make terrible parents. So it was with almost certainty I reached out and shook the slender, dagger nailed hand of Satan. - Andrew was born at 10:00pm, a healthy eight lbs four ounces, and perfect. Cathy cried, I was confused. This was not how it was supposed to happen. The baby was never supposed to have been born. Now I realized the gravity of my error, and my lack of negotiating skills. We had never discussed the timing of the deal, the Devil was going to get his money's worth so to speak. We took him home two days later, to a nursery I had begrudgingly set up within our room, and I waited. - It took longer than I had expected. Andrew was six months old when he passed away peacefully in his sleep. SIDS the doctor said, nothing we could have done to prevent it. He had just started mumming the word dada. Cathy was devastated. So was I. Surely this pain was my price, the crushing swallowing darkness as we buried our son and cried. - Cathy became distant. She had stopped eating, swapping between muttering angrily or bursting into tears. I wasn't allowed near her, she would shut herself in the room and cry about not being good enough mother. I watched as she wasted away. Eventually, she was so malnourished her organs started to fail and she had to be rushed to the hospital. This is all my fault. I was wrong, and this is all my fault. What have I done. I sat in a hospital chair surrounded by beeping machines, the ones keeping Cathy asleep and breathing. Wait, she wasn't breathing, her eyes were open and she was laughing from behind the respirator in her throat I approached her slowly, about to call the nurse. I met her eyes, and they were steel, and bored into me like knives. Her eyes never left me as she reached up and tore the tubes from her throat and body and I lunged for the bed, trying to call the nurse. I started yelling. " I hope you suffer. " Cathy hadn't spoken a clear word to me in months, and the sharpness of that simple statement froze me. " F-for what my love? " I knew. Of course Satan had told her. " For selling our son to the Devil. " And her heart stopped beating. - Edited and re-posted for many errors. I hope you enjoy it, all feedback is appreciated. Thanks for reading!

article: The differential privacy is a widely accepted conception of privacy preservation and the Laplace mechanism is a famous instance of differential privacy mechanisms to deal with numerical data. In this mechanism, random noise from the Laplace distribution is added to the original data to mask the true value, but still provide a useful and accurate approximation of the data. The level of privacy protection can be adjusted by changing the amount of noise added, and this adjustment trade-offs between data privacy and data utility. In general, more noise is added for greater privacy, but it also leads to less accurate approximations of the original data. Overall, the Laplace mechanism is an effective way to protect individual privacy while still providing useful data for research and analysis.

article: The "killer bee," AKA the Africanized honey bee, is a hybrid bee created from Western and European bee strains. For whatever reason (and I'm not a geneticist nor a beekeeper, so I don't know how this happened), the Africanized bee picked up a few nasty traits. They are excessively defensive of their hive, and will swarm much more aggressively in defense of it. They are also known to pursue more aggressively. Where normal honeybees will swarm a threat and pursue for a limited distance, returning to the hive once they feel the invader is no longer a threat, killer bees are known to swarm greater numbers of bees and will chase for a much greater distance. They're thus much more likely to inflict lethal numbers of stings than basic honeybees. Several swarms of these bees escaped captivity. The problem then became the fact that they compete more aggressively than European honeybees and tend to push them out when they compete for territory, meaning that the "killer bee" is rapidly spreading as wild swarms supplant the native wild honeybees.

The paper proposes a resource allocation scheme that can ensure the coexistence of these two service classes while meeting their performance requirements. This scheme involves dividing the available radio resources between the CS and NCS, based on their respective priority levels, and dynamically adjusting the allocation based on the network conditions. The proposed scheme also takes into account the mobility of the users and the varying network conditions that may affect the performance of the services. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is evaluated through simulations and shown to provide reliable and efficient coexistence of the CS and NCS services. article: We prove the completeness of an axiomatization for differential equation invariants. First, we show that the differential equation axioms in differential dynamic logic are complete for all algebraic invariants. Our proof exploits differential ghosts, which introduce additional variables that can be chosen to evolve freely along new differential equations. Cleverly chosen differential ghosts are the proof-theoretical counterpart of dark matter. They create new hypothetical state, whose relationship to the original state variables satisfies invariants that did not exist before. The reflection of these new invariants in the original system then enables its analysis. We then show that extending the axiomatization with existence and uniqueness axioms makes it complete for all local progress properties, and further extension with a real induction axiom makes it complete for all real arithmetic invariants. This yields a parsimonious axiomatization, which serves as the logical foundation for reasoning about invariants of differential equations. Moreover, our results are purely axiomatic, and so the axiomatization is suitable for sound implementation in foundational theorem provers. Keywords: differential equation axiomatization, differential dynamic logic, differential ghosts

article: The Web has enabled one of the most visible recent developments in education - the deployment of massive open online courses. With their global reach and often staggering enrollments, MOOCs have the potential to become a major new mechanism for learning. In a MOOC, each student's complete interaction with the course materials takes place on the Web, thus providing a record of learner activity of unprecedented scale and resolution. In this work, we use such trace data to develop a conceptual framework for understanding how users currently engage with MOOCs. We develop a taxonomy of individual behavior, examine the different behavioral patterns of high- and low-achieving students, and investigate how forum participation relates to other parts of the course. We also report on a large-scale deployment of badges as incentives for engagement in a MOOC, including randomized experiments in which the presentation of badges was varied across sub-populations. article: Software requirement analysis can certainly benefit from prevention and early detection of failures, in particular by some kind of automatic analysis. Formal methods offer means to represent and analyze requirements with rigorous tools, avoiding ambiguities and allowing automatic verification of requirement consistency. However, formalisms often clash in the culture or lack of skills of software analysts, making them challenging to apply. In this article, we propose a Domain-Specific Language (DSL) based on Set Theory for requirement analysts. The Graphical InvaRiant Language (GIRL) can be used to specify software requirement structural invariants, with entities and their relationships. Those invariants can then have their consistency evaluated by the Alloy Analyzer, based on a mapping semantics we provide for transforming GIRL models into Alloy specifications with no user intervention. With a prototypical language editor and transformations implemented into an Eclipse plugin, we carried out a qualitative study with requirement analysts working for a government software company in Brazil, to evaluate usability and effectiveness of the GIRL-based analysis of real software requirements. The participants were able to effectively use the underlying formal analysis, since 79 out of 80 assigned invariants were correctly modeled. While participants perceived as low the complexity of learning and using GIRL's simplest, set-based structures and relationships, the most complex logical structures, such as quantification and implication, were challenging. Furthermore, almost all post-study evaluations from the participants were positive, especially as a tool for discovering requirement inconsistencies.

article: Given a positive integer k, a k -dominating set in a graph G is a set of vertices such that every vertex not in the set has at least k neighbors in the set. In other words, a k-dominating set is a set of vertices that "dominates" the rest of the vertices in the graph, by having at least k connections to every vertex not in the set. For example, in a graph with k 2, a 2-dominating set would be a set of vertices such that every vertex not in the set has at least 2 neighbors in the set. K-dominating sets are important in graph theory, as they have many applications in computer science, networking, and other fields. They can be used to model situations where certain nodes in a network need to have a certain level of influence over the rest of the network, or where certain nodes need to be protected by multiple redundant connections to the rest of the network.

Given the weather and soil properties, farmers need to take critical decisions such as which seed variety to plant and in what proportion, in order to maximize productivity. These decisions are irreversible and any unusual behavior of external factors, such as weather, can have catastrophic impact on the productivity of crop. A variety which is highly desirable to a farmer might be unavailable or in short supply, therefore, it is very critical to evaluate which variety or varieties are more likely to be chosen by farmers from a growing region in order to meet demand. In this paper, we present our visual analytics tool, ViSeed , showcased on the data given in Syngenta 2016 crop data challenge 1 footnote 1 1 footnote 1 . This tool helps to predict optimal soybean seed variety or mix of varieties in appropriate proportions which is more likely to be chosen by farmers from a growing region. It also allows to analyse solutions generated from our approach and helps in the decision making process by providing insightful visualizations.

article: I'm from the UK, and where I come from, we don't identify people by their race. "African-British" is something that's unheard of, and I feel that the common practice of labelling certain races as a part of a group of "minorities" in the US rather than labelling them by their nationality is in fact encouraging social inequality in a subtle way. When you refer to a large of people entirely based on their race and they themselves do as well, it may not seem wrong. Particularly when they are given equal opportunities and equal rights as the rest of the population. However, I argue that since their identity has been linked to their race nonetheless, it in fact encourages an image of separation. When you introduce yourself, you don't say "I'm a Caucasian-American." Yet it is normal for other races to introduce themselves as "I'm African-American" or "I'm Asian-American" when we should all be saying "I'm American." Because then if all races are indistinguishable from each other and are known by their nationality, then no subtle separation of identity happens and we can say we have realised equality on a small, social scale as well as the large, fundamental scale that we've achieved in recent decades. When I talk to a "minority," I don't identify the colour of their skin as an important thing to take notice of when I later explain him or her to a friend. They're just a man or a woman. It's not complete social equality if you're referring to someone and including their race in the explanation, or they introduce themselves using their race as part of their identity when not all races engage in this. A relevant clip from a 60 Minutes interview with Morgan Freeman may explain what I'm talking about more clearly: EDIT: This got more comments and upvotes than I expected. Some of you already changed my view before this thread even hit 50 upvotes. I have a few points I need to briefly address. I originally started this thread because I'm not really wholly "British" in regards to ethnicity - I'm mixed race. Half of my family originate from Armenia in blood which means I'm half Indo-European Aryan if the official Armenia website is to be trusted] and my other half are British by blood as well (Welsh, to be specific). However, the Aryan ethnic features are not white, blonde people with blue eyes as it's thought of, due to Nazism. I've been to Armenia, it's not the case. In recent weeks, I questioned how I should be identifying myself. Am I "Armenian-British"? Am I really "Aryan-British"? Should I identify myself as just "Armenian" or "British"? Or "Aryan"? Or "Half Armenian, half British"? Which side of my family is more relevant in determining how I see myself? Then I began asking myself how I would be perceived if I identified myself using any of the labels except "British." Would I be seen as a foreigner? Would it still be equal for me to publicly identify myself something other than my nationality or mixing that with my designated race when someone describes me? If that were the case, would people subtly view or judge me differently for it or think nothing of it? Does it depend on the person who learns this? Of course, I don't hold these views now. These questions I had are what led to me to take the view that it wasn't still equal in that case - but I keep an open mind. So I asked you - and you definitely delivered in the " (literal) boatloads." To those whom express a legal concern at my former proposal, you are right. For such a thing to done, thoughts and perceptions would need to be regulated, and Orwell would be livid. When I wrote this question, I intended to pose it in a theoretical light because it was only my view. I make sure I never consider my opinion as fact or a part of me. Particularly when I'm uncertain, similar to when I asked myself all those questions. Make you define your opinions, never make your opinions define you. To quote Tzu: "Watch your words; they become actions." I recommend everyone reads [uessentialsalts] 's comment for a legal perspective on this proposal. To those who commented and were of different races, you provided a very relevant perspective on this proposal, and I thank you for providing your arguments and insight. It was invaluable in helping me CMV. Is a misunderstanding of how the income taxes work. With marginal rates, you only pay the higher tax rate on income above that amount. So if you make 50,000 and the tax rates are 10 on the first 15,000, 20 between 15,000 and 45,000, and 25 on everything above 45,000. You only pay 25 on the last 5,000, 20 on the middle 30,000 and 15 on the first 15,000. 2. Is a real concern thanks to the stupid way most welfare type programs works. Many programs are setup only to provide benefits below an income threshold, so maybe you get 2000 of food stamps if you make less than 10,000 in income. So if you make 9,999, you get an additional 2,000 in food stamps, given you an effective equivalent income of 11,999. But if you income goes up 1, you no longer qualify for food stamps, so now you effective income is 10,000. This discourages raises because people will be worst off unless the raise is high enough to offset it. This is terrible design, and could be mitigated by having a gradual reduction, i.e. you lost .50 of food stamp benefits for every dollar of income above 8,000 so that you are always noticably better off making more money.', "I never heard of that before, but if some people do that, it's because they don't understand how tax brackets work.," "People think that if they get a raise that it will push them in a higher bracket and they'll overall net less income overall. article: I'm not a cab-driver and rarely a cab customer, but when I need a cab I don't want some random guy with a car. Lyft and Uber seem to think cab-driving isn't a skill, that it's something anyone can do with no training. Well, it's not. An experienced cabbie provides a reliable service that Joe Schmoe who owns a Chevy can mimic but can't duplicate. Lyft and Uber drivers offer: Questionable insurance. Questionable character. Questionable integrity. Questionable driving safety. Questionable background checks. Questionable service for the disabled and elderly. Questionable answers to questions about the city and area. Questionable coverage at other than peak commute times. Like numerous other professions, taxi service is regulated for good reasons to prevent such questionable situations. Do-it-yourself pretend-cabs like Lyft and Uber should not be allowed to ignore the rules and regulations that real cab operators must follow. Change my view. Edit: Added deltas to my replies to several comments. And I'll add that I learned a lot in this conversation, and wouldn't make the same arguments now that I made in my original post. I've learned plenty about the way Lyft and Uber operate. My original notions were based on a few newspaper articles, not even recent articles, and I appreciate the educating. I've learned that LyftUber fans are vividly enthusiastic about the joy of riding in a stranger's car over a taxicab. It's a level of adoration I haven't seen since attending a few Grateful Dead concerts in the 1980s, but I loved that spirit then so I can't judge it harshly now. I've learned that LyftUber fans in CMV view the cab industry pretty much the same as PETA members view Oscar Meyer, and seem to believe that virtually all regulations of the taxi industry serve no public good, and exist only to protect cab operations from competition. Mostly, I've learned that CMV is a fun place to hang out on a Sunday afternoon, and that most of the debaters here play fair and don't seem to hate people for disagreeing, which is nice. article: In crowdsourcing when there is a lack of verification for contributed answers, output agreement mechanisms are often used to incentivize participants to provide truthful answers when the correct answer is hold by the majority. In this paper, we focus on using output agreement mechanisms to elicit effort, in addition to eliciting truthful answers, from a population of workers. We consider a setting where workers have heterogeneous cost of effort exertion and examine the data requester's problem of deciding the reward level in output agreement for optimal elicitation. In particular, when the requester knows the cost distribution, we derive the optimal reward level for output agreement mechanisms. This is achieved by first characterizing Bayesian Nash equilibria of output agreement mechanisms for a given reward level. When the requester does not know the cost distribution, we develop sequential mechanisms that combine learning the cost distribution with incentivizing effort exertion to approximately determine the optimal reward level.

article: We consider the problem of fitting variational posterior approximations using stochastic optimization methods. The performance of these approximations depends on (1) how well the variational family matches the true posterior distribution, (2) the choice of divergence, and (3) the optimization of the variational objective. We show that even in the best-case scenario when the exact posterior belongs to the assumed variational family, common stochastic optimization methods lead to poor variational approximations if the problem dimension is moderately large. We also demonstrate that these methods are not robust across diverse model types. Motivated by these findings, we develop a more robust and accurate stochastic optimization framework by viewing the underlying optimization algorithm as producing a Markov chain. Our approach is theoretically motivated and includes a diagnostic for convergence and a novel stopping rule, both of which are robust to noisy evaluations of the objective function. We show empirically that the proposed framework works well on a diverse set of models: it can automatically detect stochastic optimization failure or inaccurate variational approximation.

article: In machine learning, asynchronous parallel stochastic gradient descent (APSGD) is broadly used to speed up the training process through multi-workers. Meanwhile, the time delay of stale gradients in asynchronous algorithms poses a challenge to convergence. To mitigate this issue, various solutions have been proposed, such as regularization techniques, weighted updates, and delay compensation mechanisms. However, these solutions come with their own trade-offs and may incur additional computational costs. Another related challenge is ensuring the consistency of the model parameters across workers. In synchronous SGD, all workers update their parameters simultaneously, ensuring consistency. However, in asynchronous SGD, the model state can diverge across workers as they update their parameters asynchronously. One solution to this problem is to periodically synchronize the model state across workers or to use techniques such as elastic averaging SGD, which dynamically adjusts the learning rate based on the divergence of model parameters across workers. Overall, asynchronous parallel stochastic gradient descent can be a powerful technique for speeding up the training process in large-scale machine learning tasks, but careful consideration should be given to the potential issues and trade-offs.

article: The different colors are produced (more or less) by different wavelengths. It's a little bit more complicated than that since vision is complicated, but that's close enough. The green color of plants comes from chlorophyll, the chemical that allows plants to capture sunlight to produce energy. It just so happens that it's good at absorbing blue and red light, but not as good at absorbing green (which gets reflected or goes through). Strictly speaking, there are several types of chlorophyll, but most plants limit themselves to two, which are green and yellow. So what would be the most catalyzing (for growth) colour? I would speculate and say blue, since that's the color chlorophyll most strongly absorbs. But there could be other factors at play - I'm not a botanist. Bonus question: Is this the same for plants that aren't green? Most plants that aren't green still have chlorophyll of the same kind, they just have other pigments that change their color. So yes, it should be the same. There are a few exceptions: some algae and cyanobacteria use different forms of chlorophyll that are different colors and absorb different wavelengths of light, usually because they live in environments where blue light doesn't penetrate well.

article: I entered the isolated room, its size foreboding on me like I was a dwarf. All along the walls dotted several different computers, each one tasked with some different use, each one getting the humans no further to opening the spaceships hull. I was just an average smart person, working for cancer research uk I had made several breakthroughs, none of which were the cure of course, but breakthroughs nonetheless. It was 3 in the morning when the call came through. "Mr. Smith, we have a proposal for you, one of magnificent proportions and huge prospects." I squinted, my eyes still straining for the appropriate level of light as that darned street lamp from outside cast its wondrous glow in my eyes. "Who is this? how did you get my number? and its Doctor! not Mr!" "Mr. Smith." The voice said, practically telling me it wont give in to my demands so easily. "This is a top secret government agency, and you have been selected amongst millions to be part of our top secret investigation." "What top secret government agency? What top secret investigation?" I had sat up now, the curiosity had been touched, although it sounded like one of those prank calls you would get from people attempting to collect your bank details. "All will become clear to you, all you have to say is yes and you will be contractually obliged to do as we say, that includes not confessing the truth of this phone call to anyone. You are being recorded, so don't think you can back out on your word either..... let's just say it involves..... other life." I was so confused, if I said yes it could mean anything, but my life was so boring..... nobody seemed to appreciate me at work and, wait..... did she say other life? was she implying aliens? whats the worst that could happen? A lot of things really..... but I didn't get this far without taking risks. "Er..... ok." I said to them, hitting myself mentally that I didn't say yes, you're meant to sound confident and in control not submissive. "We need a yes, Mr. Smith." "Yes." I said almost instantly, god dammit. "Great Dr. Smith! be ready in 2 hours and we'll have a car waiting for you outside your house, the journey is quite a while so you'll be able to sleep in the car. The windows are blacked out anyway as our location is top secret." I was starting to regret this already. The phone went dead. Well that's charming, guess I may as well get up now and get ready lest I oversleep. That was a few hours ago, it was now 3pm in..... well I don't know where that journey was indeed rather long. Still in the country though, didn't need a plane. Unless we embarked a ferry without my knowing. I took the room in, it was too massive to comprehend really. There wasn't many staff here to say how big the room was, I guess it was as secret as they said. "Doctor Smith." A womans voice next to me called out. I turned to see a woman in her mid 40's (ish) looking very stern and serious looking in a nice crease-less suit, if I were 30 years younger..... "Ah, the woman on the phone I presume?" I asked, not actually remembering what she sounded like. "Yes, of course. Now you must understand that you can not speak about this to anyone, not even your wife or your children. Not your closest friend or your neighbors dogs former owners maids uncle, got it?" What? "er..... sure, whats the secret anyway?" She walked away from me as if she didn't hear my question. "Follow me, and mind where you're walking we have lots of..... devices on the prowl." She didn't look back at me when she spoke, she seemed very sure of herself. I followed her, she was leading me to a big tent in the middle of the room, I wondered what it was obscuring. Eventually we made it inside, and what was inside was phenomenal. It was a huge spaceship, at least to the humans it was huge. It was dark purple in colour and had lots of random straight lines running around it which seemed like small rectangular crevices in the ships structure, did they serve a purpose or were they just decorative? either way they had white light zipping through them like electricity moving from one place to another, perhaps an element we do not know about. "Stop gawking, follow me." What was going on? this was too much. "Wait." I said sternly, it seemed to work as she stopped. "What is this? is this a joke? what do you need me for?" "This is not a joke, this spacecraft was found here 12 years ago and we built this building around it to obscure it from satellites, locals and tourists. We picked you because you are smart, unbelievably smart. Nobody has ever done so much for the battle against cancer as you have." Well I wasn't expecting answers that easily. "I see you seemed quite surprised at my response, we exercise full disclosure in this work environment. Full transparency to avoid any conspiracy theories against the staff and for a full diagnostic on whatever this thing is, no data goes unmissed as far as I'm aware of. It's important to let the staff feel comfortable and safe, that way moral is higher and work is quicker and more efficient." She talked too much, at my age it was hard to keep track of what she was saying. "Ok." I responded. "That's it?" She asked, surprised. "Yes." I said, "Actually no, why exactly do you need me again?" "We are trying to open it, we can't. So we're bringing in all the smartest brains from around the world to figure it out, so far no luck." She seemed disappointed. "Well thats a bummer." I said uncaring, yes it was interesting but I just wanted to see inside, I didn't want to actually have to work with this thing. She raised an eyebrow at me. "Perhaps your insight into anatomy and biology may be useful, we're not sure how it operates and microbes, bacteria and all that stuff may be the answer. It's a long shot, but we're trying all angles." Jeez does she ever shut up? "You talk too much." There were audible gasps from around the room, clearly nobody was brave enough to stand up to this woman. "Mr. Smith! we operate a tight leash here and we will not accept insubordination of any degree! do you understand?!" Was she still talking? "Yes yes." I said now concentrating on the ship. I went to touch it when she spoke again. "We've already tried that, we tried everything. Sheer force and pressure dont seem to budge it, we can't even chip it to get a sample of the element it uses." She finally stopped talking and I went back to touch it. My hand light pressed down on the hull of the ship and the white zipping light vanished along with a powering down sound, everyone gasped again. Nothing works huh? I thought to myself. There was a momentary pause, then a slight hissing sound like some hydraulics. Heh, highly technologically advanced aliens and they use hydraulics. An outline of a door appeared where I touched the ship and a set of stairs came down with it. There was suddenly lots of shouting and my ears struggled to comprehend all the noises, some men with big guns grabbed me and shoved me to the ground telling me to not move and keep my hands where they can see them. I'm 75 years old! What am I gon na do hit them with my walking stick? perhaps my zimmer frame is a secret nuclear warhead. 3 men surrounded me, making sure I didn't move when all of a sudden they all flew back and harmlessly landed on the floor. In the door of the ship appeared a being, a human being. Ok it wasn't a human being but I can't be bothered to describe it, it wasn't anything like we've ever imagined, not that martian crap anyway. "Hello." It said, it spoke english? "We have been monitoring your kind for some time now, we have learnt your ways and your language and we have been waiting dormant for your kind to simply calm down. We have used this spaceship as a teleporter of sorts, where we would check up on you every 6 months. Your kind only seems to degrade itself the more time you are given, because of this we decided we would only take one of you with us. Someone worthy enough to be considered'nice' as you humans like to put it." Heshe whatever gender it was if it was a gender looked at me and my gawking face. "Would you like to come with us? Doctor Smith?" I was glad it used the word Doctor. "We will take you on many journeys, many adventures, many places where you can experience wonderful and amazing sights, exquisite tastes and other..... desires." That sounded wonderful, but why me? "But im an old man! I'll be dead soon perhaps you should pick one of these younger doctors?" Not that I deemed any of them worthy enough myself. "No, we will make you young again, for as long as you desire. We'll even give you the cure to cancer before you leave, does that sound good to you?" Hell yeah. "Hell yeah." I said exactly what I was thinking, it was time to say bye. "Bye guys!" I shouted to everyone before I walked on the ship. There was a bright glow and before I knew it I was being shot through the stars and space while my skin got more youthful by the second. I was going on an adventure, and I'll never be back. article: Abstract. The deterministic random walk is a deterministic process analogous to a random walk. While there are some results on the cover time of the rotor-router model, which is a deterministic random walk corresponding to a simple random walk, nothing is known about the cover time of deterministic random walks emulating general transition probabilities. This paper is concerned with the SRT-router model with multiple tokens, which is a deterministic process coping with general transition probabilities possibly containing irrational numbers. For the model, we give an upper bound of the cover time, which is the first result on the cover time of deterministic random walks for general transition probabilities. Our upper bound also improves the existing bounds for the rotor-router model in some cases.

article: Huge primes are useful in public key cryptography, specifically RSA. Basically, the reason for this is that we (collectively as human beings) know how to multiply together two numbers very efficiently. Given two numbers of essentially arbitrary size, we can compute their product in very little time. However, we do not know how to do the reverse efficiently. Given some huge number x, that is a product of two huge primes p and q (so x pq), we do not know how to factor x into p and q in a way that doesn't take an incredibly long time and by incredibly long I mean unimaginably long. Certainly longer than any human life. Various cryptosystems (RSA is the big one) are constructed in such a way that to decrypt an encrypted message without knowing the proper decryption key, you would need to factor some huge number into its two prime factors. Edit: Just noticed the article that you linked. Primes of that size are not particularly useful. The security of cryptography is basically guaranteed with much, much smaller primes. This particular result is more of a mathematical novelty than a cryptographic success.," "Huge prime numbers are useful for cryptography as multiplying them together very easy calculation to do one way and really hard to do the other. For example, 13 times 9 equals 117. That is simple to do. Let's say you make a password system that does an equation to unlock the login, and the answer has to match 117. in your system you store a person's password as 13 rather than the actual password, and then times that by 9. If it's correct, you will have 13 times 9 which equals 117. It is much safer than matching password123 to see if it directly matches password123. If someone gets into your system, they can just see everyone's password, while if you used prime number equation they would only see the number 117. Let's take it from the hackers point of view with a different number. What two prime numbers, multiplied together, equals 7781? The only one you can eliminate straight off the bat is that it can't be number 2, as it's an odd number,. Well, what happens when I divide it by three? No, I get 2593.66666..., so that isn't correct, maybe if I tried seven... The only way to find out what two prime numbers equal 7781 is to go through and divide it by every single prime number till you get a result that is also a prime number. It will take a bit of time to figure out it's 31 times 251. Longer the prime number you are dealing with, the more computational time it will take for any hackers to figure out what prime numbers are being used.," "Finding ever-larger primes is just showing off; they're already well outside the bounds of practicality. In cryptography, primes are useful because you can multiply two large primes together and let people use the resulting number to encrypt messages, and use the primes to decrypt them. Only you know the primes, and it would take an extremely long time to factor the number you shared and find them out. If you just used two random numbers, people would usually be able to use (2 and half the number), (3 and 13 the number), (5 and 15 the number) or a similar easy answer to decrypt your message.," "Some mathematical operations are easier in one direction than the reverse. article: It is a common observation that women can act and dress like men (more or less) without reproach, but that men cannot act and dress like women without criticism. Conversely, a man who wears a dress, stays home to take care of children, and likes to arrange flowers is ridiculed and even harassed. A common (usually feminist, but not always it's tough to generalize feminism) response used to explain or justify this observation is that "femininity is viewed as weak, whereas masculinity is viewed as strong; therefore, weak strong good but strong weak bad." I want to argue that this common response prevents needed discussions of masculinity by drawing the focus back to femininity and women. That is, we tend to respond to such situations by asking, as we ask in many other places, "What's wrong with how we view women?" Very rarely do we ask, on a large scale basis, "Why is masculinity so restrictive? What can we do to help young boys feel more comfortable if they don't measure up to traditional 'masculine' standards?" I believe that men are more confined than women by gender roles, and that if we continually approach that fact by attempting to change "femininity" and not "masculinity," we will fail to facilitate change. article: Nancy slowly surveyed her grandmother's room in the home. It looked more like her own bedroom during her teenage years: there were countless pictures tacked to rows of cork boards on the wall opposite the bed, only these weren't pictures of now defunct boy bands, cheap reprints of famous artists, or torn out book pages. Told in chronological order across the boards the nurses had allowed her father to hang was her Grandmother's memory. Newspaper clippings, family photos, cheap Polaroids of the house she'd never return to it was all there, painstakingly fitted together by Nancy's father. Grandmother (never Granny, never Grandma) had a very peculiar memory. When she was younger, Grandmother could recall down to the number of buttons and color of the seam what someone had been wearing on any given day. She could tell anyone who cared (or didn't) exactly what her childhood room looked like, the way her elementary school teacher styled her hair, who was in which row for the school photo. Grandmother had been very charming and loved to impress at parties whenever someone challenged her memory, most often by daring her to describe the front page of last week's Sunday paper, headlines and all. Grandmother never lost a challenge. Except when it came to Nancy. She'd been a petulant, rowdy child. Quiet yet stubborn, she'd been a dare all her own. From a young age Grandmother had been interested in charming Nancy into submission, regaling the little girl with her favorite stories, recited from memory, or painting memories for Nancy from her infancy in such vivid detail that even today, Nancy felt they really could be hers and not just some sly story. The older Nancy became the more she rebelled against Grandmother, especially when she entered school and had refused to wear dresses. Grandmother found the plain denim overalls Nancy wore daily to be silly, impractical, and worst of all ugly, and tried to coerce Nancy into dresses each weekend when she visited. One memory Nancy does have is of her seventh Christmas. That year Grandmother had bought her a deep red woolen peacoat with a large black bow at the neck. She'd hated it on sight, but Grandmother made her try it on immediately and they'd posed for a picture together in front of the tree. Grandmother would always have that memory, or so they'd thought, but she'd wanted a picture to prove to Nancy how cute she could be if she'd only act like a lady. In the picture, which Nancy now held in her hand, she was scowling, her tiny chin poking out in a pout over that ridiculous bow, while Grandmother stood proudly with one hand on her shoulder to ensure she stood still. Nancy hated that coat and never wore it after that Christmas day, a fact that Grandmother never let her forget, even if her own memory of it would eventually fade like a snapshot left in the sun. Nancy still can remember the sharp squeeze of those long, thin fingers, the perfectly manicured nails digging into her shoulder, forcing her to stand still. Nancy looked to the small, knotted form of Grandmother sleeping on the hospital bed, curled and rolled on her side underneath a thin layer of woven cotton. She felt ill at the sight not in mourning for the woman she was losing now frame by frame, but in shame for the blankness she felt instead. She turned back to the wall and worked her way down the timeline until she found that red-coat Christmas, carefully tacked the picture to the board, and left.

article: There's a lot of anti-government explanations going on, but I think the answer you're looking for is a lot easier than that. Personally, I don't believe every politician ever is corrupt. Well the problem is how you're thinking of sneaking something in. It's easy to see if someone attaches a rider that's completely against the interests of the bill or something. But what is attaching a rider, really? It's just making an amendment to the bill. And here's the thing people are allowed to revise bills. You wouldn't expect someone to have exactly one go at typing up a bill, then it has to go to vote as is, right? Obviously they should be allowed to make some changes, revisions, and have multiple drafts before they submit to be voted on. Just like how you're allowed to make multiple changes to your college thesis all that matters is what you turn in. And, unlike your college thesis, you're allowed to have multiple people work on the bill. So one guy goes to introduce a bill, and someone else says "I'm going to make this change." Someone else says "But I don't want you to." The guy making the change says "So don't vote for it." This is where "sneaking" something in comes into play. Because now, if the guy doesn't vote for it, he'll look like he's voting against the ENTIRE bill, not just one small part. Congressmembers can't pick and choose which parts of the bill they vote for. They get a yes or no vote. (Or abstain). Not a "yes to this part, no to that part." So really, it's just a matter of people taking advantage of a necessary system. We have to allow revisions to bills, which means some people can take advantage of it to revise it however they want. Another approach is the U-Net architecture, which combines convolutional and upsampling layers to gradually expand the input image into a segmentation mask. These pixel labeling approaches can be used for various applications such as medical image segmentation, semantic segmentation of outdoor scenes, and satellite image analysis. However, they may not be as accurate as the region-based methods for complex scenarios with overlapping objects and occlusions. Therefore, choosing the appropriate approach depends on the specific problem at hand and its requirements for accuracy, speed, and resource constraints.

article: It had been an astonishing week, Aquinas thought as he sat down to take a breather. The comfortable couch in his room was his favorite place to relax. A mixture of business and pleasure; he'd placed his room close to the crew center, in case of emergency, but had also great pains (mostly wounds to the wallet) to ensure he had a wall built of holoscreens, which displayed the view from the ship all around him. It was beautiful - it always was. Right now, he had a view of the star LOGLA. On the approach he'd admired its brilliance, the way the plasma arced and danced on its surface. That was before he'd spoken to it. The initial communications had been halting, uncertain. Stars had very different minds than humans, in many ways. It'd taken thousands of years to realize they were even capable of thought. It had taken hundreds to decipher their thoughts. The stars, it turned out, had similar difficulties understanding us. We were motes of dust to them, insignificant in the passage of time. The stars - communicating on their own medium still largely inaccessible to us, the'sea' as they called it - had debated the significance of humans ever since we'd left our atmosphere. The lines between the animate and the inanimate had been blurred. Stars saw all things as living, in some sense - some more so than others, of course. Stars did not quite propagate, or survive. They simply..... were, until they weren't. And they thought for that entire time. To the stars, it turns out, they'd just assumed we were intelligent. They assumed all things were intelligent. Perhaps not capable of communication or comprehension, but still possibly thinking on some plane of existence. "They are, therefore they think." It was a compelling point of view, all things considered. If we could talk to stars, why not to other things? Aquinas sighed, as he shifted in his chair to get back up. Only a moment's rest. The basic politics has been discussed, the nature of stars, what they wanted and did not want..... it had been largely business. There'd been moments of insight and true talk, here and there, but for the most part it was the simple procedure of extraterrestrial contact the System's scientists had sorted out centuries before. Stars were independent bodies, but didn't much care about anything else - they felt no pain, and did not care what installations we built around them, or how we traversed them. The only thing they requested was that they be allowed to think, as long as possible. Aquinas rose from his chair, and crossed the room. The auxiliary controls in his room had been another nice touch. Built for emergencies, but..... it's not like what he was about to do could hurt. He reached down, fiddled with some controls - that transmitted very complicated directions to a very big machine on the ship - and was linked into the communication medium, a swirling ball of plasma that was magnetically controlled to produce new shapes, configurations, and energy patterns. After a moment in silence, standing over the controls, bowed with his hands flat against the surface of the countertop, he spoke up. "Logla, you listening?" He asked. The star had no name. No stars did. It had agreed on one, however, given the nature of human communication. So it had been decided to name it Logla, and the star agreed that when we said Logla, it would answer. And it did. "I'm here, Aquinas." He piqued up at this, as he always did. It recognized him, despite the communication medium - and the fact he hadn't said much of note. There was some other means of identification..... which was surprising, given stars had no need for such identification. A quick learner, it seemed. "What thoughts do we have to attend to?" Aquinas chuckled. Stars did little else but think, so Logla had an issue phrasing any activity as something other than thinking. It understood the activities, well enough, but it just preferred not to speak of them in human terms. "Nothing to attend to, today, Logla. I just wanted to think together." A soft humming came from the speaker. This indicated the star was processing, preparing to vocalize thoughts. A very human mannerism. Eventually, Logla spoke up. "This sounds agreeable. It is something stars do often, and enjoy." "Enjoy? You don't talk about emotion a lot, Logla. To be honest..." Aquinas pondered whether to continue, but shrugged and went on anyway. "We weren't quite sure you felt things like we did. You know, felt them as much." The star hummed again. "Most likely not, Aquinas. But we still feel. Feeling is just another form of thinking, after all." Aquinas smiled. "That's one way of putting it," Aquinas sat back down in his chair, no longer nervous about how poorly unsupervised contact might go. Logla was a very nice star, so far. It was pretty damn unlikely he'd upset it. He wasn't even sure what could. At this thought, Aquinas sat, tapped his chin, then pressed the button to continue speaking. "What makes you feel, Logla? And what do you feel?" The star hummed, for a long time. At least a minute. This was unusual - most thoughts took stars very little time, because they had very, very big brains. Finally, the star continued, "Everything makes me feel, Aquinas. How could it not? Stars have a long time to think..... and with a long time, everything becomes worth thinking about," The star hummed shortly, then continued, "I feel..... happy. Sad. Curious." Aquinas raised an eyebrow. "Not afraid? Not angry?" "Those are unintelligible to me. Rethink your thoughts for me, Aquinas?" This was a fun oddity of inter-species communication. Stars rarely did not understand each other, they had learned - it was only external interference that caused issues with communication. Logla did not quite understand the idea of'untranslatable' concepts yet - but it very well understood interference, and just acted like it was that. "Well, anger..... it's..... when something is wrong. Or when something endangers you. Do you ever feel so strongly, you want to..." Aquinas realized that there wasn't really much the star could do, or want to do. Stars could not move. They could not act. They could barely even perceive, it turned out. article: I had always considered myself an open minded and progressive individual, which initially was one of the reasons that made me move from the desolate countryside village I grew up in and into the vast metropolis Nhew Y'ork was nowadays. I sighed - in my head only, considering my boss could and would pick up on the scent of the air leaving my mouth. Plus he was the type to not only comment but be offended by it. I turned around and faced the large reptilian man just in time to witness his split tongue slithering out and back into his mouth in a fraction of a second. "Yes Mr. Iguano I am, I..... I was just lost in thought." His narrow pupils, framed by an iris in the color of brown desert sand, narrowed even further and I hastily added: "Sir. Here's your coffee, sir." Though the label coffee mostly was for identifying the purpose of the drink only it still was a fitting name for the grey, muddy beverage in my book. His tongue darted out of his mouth as if he considered saying something, but then he simply took the mug and turned towards the window the have a few silent sips in the sunshine that made its way into the room through the shutters. Tension I hadn't realised I had accumulated left my body noticeably. "Do you have another task for me, Sir?" I asked him to which he only waved lazily. I was free to go. Upon closing the door I sighed again, this time for real and started to make my way towards the break room. I realised I still had the second mug in my hand and took a sip myself - it was real coffee for me though. At my destination I was pleasantly surprised to see Seri - a humanoid with brilliant yellow feathers covering her slim, agile body. She turned around as I entered the room and her small beak moved in a fashion I had come to recognize as a smile. I blushed a little out of habit because I had had a mild crush on her for the last few months until I had decided to move on. "Heya Charlie. How's it going?" she chirped, literally. Some of the avians, especially the songbird kind, had that really melodic way of speaking. It was fascinating and distracting at the same time. And me still liking her to some degree didn't help on that front. "Hey Seri. Not much really. Mr. Iguano is terrifying as always and I don't have much to do apart from getting copies or some kind of brew for some kind of min..." I stopped. I had meant to say minx which was slang for the new-age races but kind of..... racist? "Sorry. " , I said. She hadn't stopped "smiling." I guess she'd had to deal with worse. And now that I thought about it I couldn't help but wonder which generation of her ancestors went sentient. It was different for every species. "Don't worry Charlie, you've got my permission to use that word. After all you're my little minx!" "Urgh, please no I beg you." Too late, she was already getting a kick out of it. "Oh but you're me wittle human and I..." Luckily she was forced to stop there, as her superior entered the room. Or forced himself into it more like as he had to duck through the door, which already was more like a gate than a door. His ill fitting suit stretched dangerously thin over the huge muscles covered in thick black fur. As with most sentients his species had gotten bigger when they evolved. Only that gorillas had been considerably big to begin with. "Ms. Flavi, sorry to..." he stopped to cough violently and I had to grab and hold my mug as the table shook in rhythm. He then proceeded fumble with a small paper box trying to get one of the cigarettes out which seemed incredibly tiny compared to his huge paws. "Sorry to interrupt your break but you're needed in the SA-Department. Some new hawk type and nobody understands him and I think..." He coughed again, less violent now that he somehow had managed to light his cig. "I think they classified him a PSC 3 so be careful." Seri just nodded, gave me an apologetic look and went on her way. I was left with Mr. Gorilla. Whose last name was kind of the equivalent in genericness to a Mr. Smith, but I never understood why that was an appropriate comparison. I had yet to meet someone called Mr. or Mrs. Human. Mr. Gorilla glared at me and continued chain-smoking. I was only the intern after all. The small human trainee in the A.R.E.S.E. - the Administration for recently evolved sentient entities. - The day passed slowly, as any day did in the bureau. I guess you couldn't expect any excitement to be had as the intern, but still after 3 months of being the general drudge I was at the point of throwing the towel. Oh how I yearned to at least be able to sneak a peek at Seris job. She was working in the sentient assimilation department which handled the task of working with newly sentient beings - beings who had awoken as people called it. But, contrary to what one would assume when hearing about accelerated evolution triggers, those didn't apply to an entire species at a time but happened seemingly at random. Sometimes a lot of individual animals awoke - like in the Yukon incident, where several moose gained consciousness only to be massacred by another recently awoken pack of wolves who didn't have their instincts in check yet. One of the reasons ARESE was founded. And sometimes it only happened to a single individual. Which then lead to some really depressing stories like that of the now accomplished philosopher M. Aldabra, who awoke to realize he was not only the lone conscious representative of his species but also that the latter was nearly extinct. Not that the world wasn't being swarmed with new intelligent beings every day. Official estimates assumed the number of new unique sentient life was in the dozens every week for the last two decades. And thus far only the Chordates - the major group including mammals, birds and reptiles - had had awoken cases. Overpopulation had already been a problem but know it was through the roof - quite literally because interestingly enough where skyscraper buildings were at an all time high, some of the avian species had started constructing sophisticated nest-like complexes on roofs in heavily populated areas. Furthermore there was an entire department in the ARESE whose only job was to plan and prepare for the worst case scenario: when the Invertebrates would start to awaken. Which then would include every insect-species, outnumbering the other races by the tens of thousands. It was a scary thought indeed. I tried not to dwell on it for too long, because while I wasn't exactly insectophobic I did get a bit squeamish when confronted with a larger amount of those pesky little multi pods. The sun, unseen by me in the vast corridors of the ARESE headquarters for the last hours, had progressed quite a bit and was tinting the streets of Manhattan in gold. Quite a few reptile-type guys were sitting in the last glow of our star to warm their bodies bevore it would be gone for the night. Some of them really had a hard time with regular work schedules because of the need for external warming and labor unions were pushing for regulations on that front. The unions in general really had a lot to do these days with new workplace needs arising every week and a ton of discrimination cases. But still the streets were bustling with activity and that would only increase once the nocturnals got up. I strolled in the general direction of my apartment and was planning to stop for groceries along the way. It was quite a few blocks I would have to walk but even after all the weeks I had already spent in the city there was still a spectacle to be witnessed around every corner. A big feline-type vendor was in the process of apologizing profoundly to a small amphibian customer at his stall for something I could only guess relating to the grilled frogs on a stick the cat was selling. It seemed that one bird of prey, a hawk maybe, was especially good at whatever he was doing because an owl-type girl was moon-eyeing him with the kind of expression only a teenager in love could make. article: Batch normalization (BN) has become a standard technique for training the modern deep networks. However, its effectiveness diminishes when the batch size becomes smaller, since the batch statistics estimation becomes less accurate. This can lead to unstable training and poor generalization performance. To address this issue, there are several techniques that can be used when dealing with smaller batch sizes, such as: 1. Group normalization: This technique replaces the batch normalization layers with group normalization layers, which divide the channels into smaller groups to compute the normalization statistics, thereby decreasing the sensitivity to batch size. 2. Layer normalization: This technique normalizes the features of each layer independently. Unlike batch normalization, which computes statistics over all examples in a batch, layer normalization computes statistics over the channels of each feature map, which makes it suitable for small batch sizes. 3. Instance normalization: This technique normalizes the features of each instance (or sample) independently. This is particularly useful in tasks such as style transfer, where the aim is to preserve the style of the input while changing its content. 4. Virtual batch normalization: This technique normalizes each example in a batch with respect to a reference batch that is computed once at the beginning of training. This reduces the dependency on batch size and can lead to improved results. Overall, the choice of normalization technique depends on the specific requirements of the task at hand and the available hardware resources.

" Come have some tea with your grandma, dearie! " the old hag called from the kitchen in a sing-song tone. Many would find the quivering voice cheery and cute. I loathed it. I smiled despite the knot in my stomach. " One moment, grandma! " Meanwhile, my fingers flew across my phone's screen. After seventeen texts and nine calls, I was getting the hint that my mom was ignoring me. Sighing, I shook my head as her words from the car ride reverbed in my head. Spend some time with your grandmother. She's really a nice lady when you get to know her. You're just too paranoid After another round of six passive aggressive texts, the sound of slippers sliding against linoleum pulled my attention away from my phone. Grandma stood in the door to the kitchen, doe-eyed. Her wrinkled lips were turned down in the slightest of frowns. I had to admit, she could put on a convincing show. No wonder everyone thought I blindly hated her. " Are you alright, dearie? " she asked in a soft tone. I faked another smile. " Yeah. Sorry, I was trying to make a call. " " Oh it's alright, " she said. She shuffled around and gestured me to follow. " But come and get your tea before it gets cold. " Sighing, I stood and trailed behind her. A part of me wanted to stab her in the back, or sweep her off her feet and claim she fell. Maybe she'd break a hip, and then have to stay in the hospital for a while. Anything to prolong her schemes before she finally succeeded. Grandma sat at the small but humble table with a slight oomph. Steaming cups of tea sat in front of her and the only other chair available. Eyeing the woman, I sat with care. It had been a while since a chair had conveniently had " a few screws loose ." As if she didn't notice, Grandma blew into her cup before taking a sip. She continued to do so in agonizing silence, the ticking clock the only other source of noise. After five minutes, she nodded towards me with a furrowed brow. " Do you not like tea? " she asked. " I can never remember if it's you or Sean that doesn't like tea. " " I am Sean, Grandma, " I said with a frown. " But I think something may be wrong with my tea. " " Oh? How so? Not enough sugar? " I narrowed my eyes. " You know what you did. You poisoned it. " Learning how to sniff out poisons in my food and drink was essential when staying with Grandma. After the last time I had nearly died from an alleged stomach flu, I prepared myself but not being able to detect not only common but even the most obscure poisons. Even the most subtle weren't enough to catch me off guard anymore. Grandma recoiled, eyes open in shock. " I would never poison you! " " Cut the bullshit. I'm on to you. You're not going to kill me this time unless you get a little more creative. " I expected Grandma to drag out the dramatics a little longer. After all, she never broke character. This time, however, she rose from her chair with a frightening scowl. Must have been because she knew her clock was ticking. " Don't get fucking comfortable, " she barked as she stormed away. " I'll see you at dinner, you little shit. "

article: This paper introduces a novel method for learning how to play the most difficult Atari 2600 games from the Arcade Learning Environment using deep reinforcement learning. The proposed method, called human checkpoint replay , consists in using checkpoints sampled from human gameplay as starting points for the learning process. This is meant to compensate for the difficulties of current exploration strategies, such as -greedy, to find successful control policies in games with sparse rewards. Like other deep reinforcement learning architectures, our model uses a convolutional neural network that receives only raw pixel inputs to estimate the state value function. We tested our method on Montezuma's Revenge and Private Eye, two of the most challenging games from the Atari platform. The results we obtained show a substantial improvement compared to previous learning approaches, as well as over a random player. We also propose a method for training deep reinforcement learning agents using human gameplay experience, which we call human experience replay.

article: Most work in algorithmic fairness to date has focused on discrete outcomes, such as deciding whether to grant someone a loan or not. In these classification settings, group fairness criteria such as independence, separation and sufficiency can be measured directly by comparing rates of outcomes between subpopulations. Many important problems however require the prediction of a real-valued outcome, such as a risk score or insurance premium. In such regression settings, measuring group fairness criteria is computationally challenging, as it requires estimating information-theoretic divergences between conditional probability density functions. This paper introduces fast approximations of the independence, separation and sufficiency group fairness criteria for regression models from their (conditional) mutual information definitions, and uses such approximations as regularisers to enforce fairness within a regularised risk minimisation framework. Experiments in real-world datasets indicate that in spite of its superior computational efficiency our algorithm still displays state-of-the-art accuracy fairness tradeoffs.

The methodology is useful for energy-constrained wireless sensor networks, IoT applications, and smart grid systems, where energy conservation is a critical challenge.
