article: It's just the rain, I had told myself as I grabbed my hat and coat before leaving my office. It's just the rain, I had told myself as I walked down the stairs from the 67th floor, sweating in the damp tropical heat of the wet season. It's just the rain, I said as I walked out of the rundown tenement building where I lived and worked and into the partially flooded downtown streets. And now, as I leaned against a building, my coat and hat soaked through, raindrops the size of my fist pelting my back, I told myself again, it's just the rain. Oh the lies we tell ourselves. Little worlds of comfort we build from meaningless words, spun into islands of pointless optimism, ultimately dashed against the rocks of the cold, hard reality of the situation. It's never just rain. Not in Bangkok in June. Not anymore. The city floodwalls had broken during the last wet season and corrupt officials saw to it that they were never fixed, pocketing the baht set aside for repairs. The immediate result was a city that flooded four months out of the year, and the worlds largest mosquito breeding grounds. Uncomfortable though they were, the high boots, long coat, and hat served the dual purpose of providing the illusion of comfort in a monsoon and preventing your poor protagonist from being eaten alive. People tended not to hang around outside in the wet season. I'd been standing here for four long, wet hours. Amazing what you'll do for five thousand baht a day, plus expenses. A barely living wage with the amount of clients I get these days. Once upon a time, I would never have taken the case. Missing persons cases are trouble. Nine times out of ten, it's a cheating spouse run off with the secretary. The other time, it's police business. That was in Chicago. Another city, another continent, another life. Here and now, there was no such thing as police business. Police business meant that your chances of seeing that person in one piece again were marginal at best. The police had been bought by the Three Phi ring a decade ago. And my client had paid twenty thousand baht up front. A small fortune and last months rent. All I had to do was track the girl, and report next Wednesday. An air taxi blew past, pink neon sign flickering, air cushion kicking up a wall of water at me. For a moment I was distracted and almost missed her make her move. A slim girl in a wide brimmed hat disappeared around a corner and I hurried after her. I rounded the corner just in time to watch her climb into an expensive private aircar. The door was being held open by a man I recognized by reputation. Suchart Prachanat. Regional narcotics distributor for the Three Phi. One of the most dangerous men in Bangkok. He must have noticed me because a gun appeared in his hand like a magic trick and he sent a half dozen flechette rounds into my chest. They pulled away as I picked myself up off my soggy ass and pulled the flechette rounds out of my long coat where they'd stuck into layered carbon nanoweave. Things had gotten complicated. I hate complicated. And it was still raining.

article: The Morton- or z -curve is one example for a space filling curve: Given a level of refinement L N 0, it maps the interval [ 0, 2 d L) to a curve that visits every point in a d-dimensional space with coordinates between 0 and 1. The Morton curve is constructed by interleaving the d binary representations of the coordinates of each point, with the most significant bit first. This creates a one-dimensional sequence of bits that can be turned into a path by interpreting every two bits as a direction (00 left, 01 down, 10 up, 11 right) in a binary tree. The resulting path visits each point in the space in a compact and efficient way, allowing for efficient spatial indexing and query operations.

article: I sniffed as I shrugged my pack a little higher on my back. From the top of this hill, I could just see the grey stone tower in the distance. With the setting sun reflecting off it, it was almost pretty. " Almost, " I laughed shortly. ' Almost'was how close I had been to making the biggest trade deal of my life. A unique delicacy, a niche in the market, a food I had served to the King himself, and was well on the way to making the most fashionable new cuisine at the court - and instead of the hefty golden compensation I had been hoping for, I was ' rewarded'by being chosen to cross the length of the Kingdom and fight a dragon practically bare-handed. " It is an honour, " I had said as I swept a low bow towards the throne, seething inside. I wasn't entirely sure if this was a calculated insult, or whether the King and his advisors just had no regard for my carefully arranged business dealings. What was it to them if some other trader moved in on my customers, my suppliers, even my favourite spot at the city market? I was just a grubby, low-class merchant to them, I supposed. I continued on miserably, feeling sorry for myself and berating the world around me. All too soon darkness closed in and the air grew chill. I made camp at the edge of the road, just enough into the woods to avoid prying eyes. With a stone for a pillow, I drew my blanket around myself and curled up to get what sleep I could. It was around noon the next day when I came to the tower itself. I had stopped briefly at the base of the hill, looking upwards with dread, and slightly loosening my sword in its scabbard. What was the point of the sword?! I thought desperately. I've never been taught the first thing about sword-fighting. I trudged upwards as if approaching a gallows. The tower itself was surrounded by a rather delicate garden, full of the kind of flowers that I would derisively have called ' pretty'had I seen them on a ceramic tea-set. Here, they just looked oddly out of place. A dark wooden door stood imposingly in the side of the tower. I noted that there was no moat, and in fact a gently sloped path ran neatly up to the door. Still, there seemed little necessity for outside protection when everybody knew there was a dragon guarding the tower. Not even an army would attempt to siege this place. Closing my eyes and giving myself up for dead, I raised a hand and knocked three times. The door creaked open. " Yes? " said a voice expectantly. Stupidly, I still had my eyes closed. I opened them to find a fairly short, blond-haired girl, perhaps in her late teens. She had two braids, one on each side of her head, and wore a plain, pale blue gown, made of some kind of home-spun material. " Uh, " I pronounced eloquently. I had not been expecting a serving girl. I coughed. " I have come to save the princess! " I announced triumphantly. I don't know what I had been expecting. Perhaps a gasp, or even a gratifying swoon - anything that would make me feel as brave as I was trying to act. I had not expected the bright, tinkling laughter I received. " Save me from what? " she gasped out between giggles. I blinked at her groggily, making my second impression as good as my first. " What? Not you, the princess. " She smiled at me. " I am the princess. Now, from what terror exactly do you think you need to rescue me? " " The... the dragon? " I asked tentatively. This was clearly one of my best days. She laughed again. " Dragon! " she called into the darkness behind her. " Dragon! " My eyes widened and I dreamed of running away even as I stood frozen to the spot in fear. She must have found a way to control this thing. Perhaps she fed it on the bones of would-be rescuers. I swallowed as I heard its scuttling feet come towards me. She opened the door wider - perhaps its jaws won't fit through the gap, I thought frantically. I flinched as a shaggy blond mass hurled itself at the princess. " Who's a good boy? Who's a good boy? " she cooed as she crouched down to embrace the Labrador. She looked up at me as she patted the dog's side and its tail wagged appreciatively. " This is Dragon, " she said simply. " Would you like to come inside? There's a kettle on the stove and I'm sure you have a lot of questions ."

article: Background: Overweight and obesity are an increasing phenomenon worldwide. Predicting future overweight or obesity early in the childhood reliably could enable a successful intervention by experts. While a lot of research has been done using explanatory modeling methods, capability of machine learning, and predictive modeling, in particular, remain mainly unexplored. In predictive modeling models are validated with previously unseen examples, giving a more accurate estimate of their performance and generalization ability in real-life scenarios. Objective: To find and review existing overweight or obesity research from the perspective of employing childhood data and predictive modeling methods. Methods: The initial phase included bibliographic searches using relevant search terms in PubMed, IEEE database and Google Scholar. The second phase consisted of iteratively searching references of potential studies and recent research that cite the potential studies. Results: Eight research articles and three review articles were identified as relevant for this review. Conclusions: Prediction models with high performance either have a relatively short time period to predict orand are based on late childhood data. Logistic regression is currently the most often used method in forming the prediction models. In addition to child's own weight and height information, maternal weight status or body mass index was often used as predictors in the models. Keywords: predictive models, machine learning, artificial intelligence, obesity, overweight

article: In this paper, using the stochastic geometry theory, we present a framework for analyzing the performance of device-to-device (D2D) communications underlaid uplink (UL) cellular networks. In our analysis, we consider a D2D mode selection criterion based on an energy threshold for each user equipment (UE). Specifically, a UE will operate in a cellular mode, if its received signal strength from the strongest base station (BS) is large than a threshold b. Otherwise, it will operate in a D2D mode. Furthermore, we consider a generalized log-normal shadowing in our analysis. The coverage probability and the area spectral efficiency (ASE) are derived for both the cellular network and the D2D one. article: The 18th Amendment was the result of decades of campaigning by temperance groups. While there had been anti-alcohol groups in America basically since the first settlers, a few thing came together in the late 19th and early 20th centuries that gave the temperance movement the momentum it needed. The main factor was the rise of evangelical Christianity, which often preached that drinking was a sin. Also, many middle-class Americans (especially women) saw drinking as a moral failing and associated it with urbanization, immigration, and industrialization. By the early 20th century, temperance groups had become very influential in national politics. They argued that alcohol was the cause of many social problems, such as crime, poverty, and domestic violence. The Anti-Saloon League, which was the most powerful of these groups, succeeded in getting many local and state governments to adopt "dry" laws, which prohibited the sale and consumption of alcohol. This was seen as a way to reduce the power of saloon owners and corrupt politicians who they claimed were in league with them. When World War I began in 1914, the temperance groups took advantage of the patriotic fervor and linked their cause to national defense. They claimed that using grain to make alcohol was unpatriotic because it took food away from the troops. In 1917, President Woodrow Wilson supported the idea of a constitutional amendment to prohibit alcohol, and in 1919, the 18th Amendment was ratified, making the manufacture, sale, and transportation of alcohol illegal in the United States.

The choice of architecture depends on the network requirements and the available resources. article: Palmprints are emerging as a new entity in multi-modal biometrics for human identification and verification. Multispectral palmprint images captured in the visible and infrared spectrum not only contain the wrinkles and ridge structure of a palm, but also the underlying pattern of veins; making them a highly discriminating biometric identifier. In this paper, we propose a feature encoding scheme for robust and highly accurate representation and matching of multispectral palmprints. To facilitate compact storage of the feature, we design a binary hash table structure that allows for efficient matching in large databases. Comprehensive experiments for both identification and verification scenarios are performed on two public datasets - one captured with a contact-based sensor (PolyU dataset), and the other with a contact-free sensor (CASIA dataset). Recognition results in various experimental setups show that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Error rates achieved by our method (0.003 on PolyU and 0.2 on CASIA) are the lowest reported in literature on both dataset and clearly indicate the viability of palmprint as a reliable and promising biometric. All source codes are publicly available.

article: Compressive sensing (CS) is a promising technology for realizing energy-efficient wireless sensors for long-term health monitoring. Experimental results upon ECG signals show that the proposed method, at a compression ratio of 10x, successfully reduces the isometry constant of the trained sensing matrices by 86 against random matrices and improves the overall reconstructed signal-to-noise ratio by 15dB over conventional model-driven approaches.

article: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has shown great potentials in finding a better neural network design than human design. Sample-based NAS is the most fundamental method aiming at exploring the search space of architectures by evaluating a finite or infinite number of architecture samples. Instead of requiring the human experts to design the network architecture, sample-based NAS can automatically search through a large space of possible architectures and find the optimal one that suits the problem at hand. Sample-based NAS algorithms typically use a reinforcement learning framework, where the architecture of the neural networks is treated as the policy, and the accuracy of the network on a given task is the reward. The algorithm repeatedly samples a set of architectures and trains them on the task to evaluate their performance. The best-performing architecture is then used to generate new ones, leading to an iterative process that gradually converges to the optimal architecture. While sample-based NAS has shown promising results in various applications such as computer vision and natural language processing, it still poses challenges such as high computational cost and instability in performance. Researchers are working on developing more efficient and stable sample-based NAS algorithms to overcome these limitations and make NAS more accessible for various practical applications.

article: We study the problem of testing identity against a given distribution with a focus on the high confidence regime. More precisely, given samples from an unknown distribution p over n -dimensional vectors, the goal is to decide between the null hypothesis that p is identical to a known distribution q, versus the alternative that the distance between p and q is large. To achieve high confidence, we use the framework of hypothesis testing with approximate randomization (HTRA), which involves two main steps: (1) constructing a test statistic that measures the distance between p and q, and (2) performing an approximate randomization test to obtain a p-value. The test statistic is typically chosen to be a distance metric such as the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic or the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) between p and q. The approximate randomization test involves randomly perturbing the samples from p to create null distributions, and computing the test statistic under these null distributions to estimate the p-value. The HTRA framework provides a flexible and powerful approach for testing identity against a given distribution, and has been successfully applied in many settings such as genetics, finance, and machine learning.

article: Hidden Markov chains are widely applied statistical models of stochastic processes, from fundamental physics and chemistry to finance, health, and artificial intelligence. The hidden Markov processes they generate are notoriously difficult to analyze, but also extremely powerful for a variety of applications. They are used for tasks such as speech recognition, time series analysis, natural language processing, and genomic sequence analysis. In a hidden Markov model, a system's state is not observed directly, but rather through a series of observations that are probabilistically related to the underlying state. The model consists of a set of hidden states, each with an associated probability distribution over observations, and a set of transition probabilities describing how the system evolves from one state to another over time. His pristine, white suit was of a cut that the mage had never seen. A god, one whose true name had been lost to the ages, one of war and commerce, loomed above him. The man-beast grasped the empty robes at Dunstan's feet, as though reading something in its very threading. "You may call me Roman," he sneered. article: Many AI researchers are publishing code, data and other resources that accompany their papers in GitHub repositories. article: I hope we can all agree that a person is entitled to reap the rewards of their labor. Most of you have likely been raised under a system of capitalism that promotes this tenet. It is for this reason that you find quite a bit of socialism prevalent in America despite the fact that our nation reveres capitalism and democracy. The next logical question with regards to estate taxes is whether or not the family of a successful capitalist is entitled to the rewards of the deceased person's labor. The notion that a select few people deserve to live a life of luxury simply because their ancestors were brilliant capitalists makes little sense to me and I don't see how it benefits society. And to be fair, levying estate taxes on dead wealthy people doesn't violate their rights... because they're dead. On the other hand, I suppose it violates their heirs' right to the pursuit of happiness? That seems like a stretch. I suppose you also have the right to be secure in your property, but where was the right to your dead relatives' property ever established? Sure, the tradition of inheritance predates written history, but it has never been a right. In fact, many inheritance traditions are incredibly prejudicial, such as only allowing the firstborn son to inherit all of the wealth. Income inequality and wealth disparity [have been proven to be detrimental to a society] . The greater the gap, the more desperate the poor become, and it is only human for desperate people to take desperate actions. The ultra rich will tell you that there is a "trickle down effect" from their coffers, but history has shown us just what a trickle it truly is. I speculate that when you have a disproportionate amount of the money supply controlled by a tiny fraction of the population, the velocity of money will drop because the rich will not be actively using as high a proportion of their wealth as the average person. Any economist will agree that slow money velocity makes for poor economic health. One major point regarding estate taxes that many people seem to miss is what they really are - they are a completely different animal from income tax, sales tax, and property tax. Estate taxes are quite simply forced wealth redistribution. The problem I have is not with wealth redistribution itself, but that the money collected by the government is not distributed directly to the least wealthy, or even to programs that aid the less fortunate. In my opinion any taxes collected from estates should ONLY be allocated to social programs such as social security, healthcare, and education. It is reprehensible for money to be taken from a deceased individual and be used to fund military actions that result in the deaths of other humans. Finally, there is longstanding historical precedent for limiting inheritance and it should be noted that the current generational transfers of wealth are greater than they have ever been historically. In ancient times, funeral rites for lords and chieftains involved significant wealth expenditure for sacrifices to religious deities, feasting, and ceremonies. The well-to-do were literally buried or burned along with most of their wealth. These traditions may have been imposed by religious edict but they served a real purpose. To this end, we implement AutoPhase 3 footnote 3 3 footnote 3: a framework that takes a program and uses deep reinforcement learning to find a sequence of compilation passes that minimizes its execution time. Without loss of generality, we construct this framework in the context of the LLVM compiler toolchain and target high-level synthesis programs. We use random forests to quantify the correlation between the effectiveness of a given pass and the program's features. This helps us reduce the search space by avoiding phase orderings that are unlikely to improve the performance of a given program. We compare the performance of AutoPhase to state-of-the-art algorithms that address the phase-ordering problem. In our evaluation, we show that AutoPhase improves circuit performance by 28 when compared to using the -O3 compiler flag, and achieves competitive results compared to the state-of-the-art solutions, while requiring fewer samples. article: The fuzzy K -means problem is a generalization of the classical K -means problem to soft clusterings, i.e. clusterings where each points belongs to each cluster to some degree. Although the classical K-means problem assigns each point to a single cluster, the fuzzy K-means problem assigns each point to all clusters with degrees of membership representing how likely the point belongs to each cluster. In fuzzy K-means, the objective is to minimize the sum of squared distances between each point and its cluster center, weighted by the degree of membership. The membership function is updated iteratively until convergence is reached. Fuzzy K-means has several advantages over classical K-means, including the ability to handle overlapping clusters and the ability to assign points to multiple clusters simultaneously. article: In this paper we present various distributed algorithms for LP-type problems in the well-known gossip model. LP-type problems include many important classes of problems such as (integer) linear programming, geometric optimization, and network flow problems. Our algorithms for LP-type problems in the gossip model utilize the dual decomposition technique, where the original problem is transformed into its dual form and then distributed among the nodes. Each node solves a local subproblem and the solutions are iteratively updated using the communication protocol until a global optimum is reached. We also introduce a novel algorithm for the distributed optimization of separable convex functions in the gossip model. This algorithm utilizes the concept of coordinate descent, where at each iteration, a single variable is updated while keeping the others fixed. The proposed algorithm achieves a linear convergence rate and outperforms existing distributed optimization algorithms in terms of convergence speed and scalability. Finally, we present simulation results that demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of our algorithms for LP-type problems and separable convex optimization in the gossip model. We provide two innovations that aim to turn VB into a robust inference tool for Bayesian neural networks: first , we introduce a novel deterministic method to approximate moments in neural networks, eliminating gradient variance; second , we introduce a hierarchical prior for parameters and a novel Empirical Bayes procedure for automatically selecting prior variances. Here are a few of the most common methods. 1. 3rd Party Dynamic Ad Service (such as Google Adsense) - This is where a domain owner takes a pre-set code from an ad-serving company to dynamically generate ads (the advertiser and website where the ad displays are never in contact). Adblock prevents most of these ads from serving, and does in fact cut revenue for the owner. These are called dynamic ads because the ad that is served changes based on a few different criteria. The domain owner can specify generic categories to show or hide ads from (eg: housing, technology, video games. Interesting note - certain categories often pay more than others, technology is one of the highest paying) Adsense will detect if you have any stored cookies in your browser, which it will use to serve ads for that specific website's product. Notice If you start google searching "Battlefield 3" and visiting websites about it, you will suddenly start seeing advertisements for it on the sites you visit. It's not coincidence! 2. Text Link Ads - In this advertising method, one website contacts another directly and requests a basic text link to be placed on a certain page (generally the home page). This form of "advertising" will not be stopped by adblock, and in turn does not cut revenue. The only kicker is that most text link advertisements are paid up front rather than whether or not a user clicks on it, so even if Adblock somehow found a way to prevent them, it wouldn't cut revenue. Note: A lot of text link ads are purchased for SEO rather than actually linking visitors to a site (basically they're buying higher google rankings) 3. Static Advertisements - Adblock will block certain types of static advertisements and will not block others. With static ads, a company contacts a website directly and gives them a code to place on the webpage. Most commonly these will appear in the sidebar (some blocked, some not), as pop-ups (blocked), or even taking up the entire background page of an image (not blocked). These advertisements are generally only seen on larger websites. Now even though Adblock prevents an advertisement from showing, the website still benefits from you visiting it. It costs more to advertise on a website with more traffic. By visiting that website you increase it's traffic, and in turn you're making the website more desirable for higher paying ads! Personally, I love Adblock because it can help a user enjoy a website more. Exploiting this close link between these two model classes and some newly observed similarities, we propose a new supervised learning framework with close similarities to logistic regression, low-rank matrix completion and neural networks. We validate the structured log-odds modelling approach in synthetic experiments and English Premier League outcomes, where the added expressivity yields the best predictions reported in the state-of-art, close to the quality of contemporary betting odds.

article: Lawyer here! This case presents a great opportunity to look at abandonment and salvage law. The bottom line is that Spain - which owned the ship and cargo in question - never abandoned its ownership interest. In order for a person to abandon property, that person must exhibit some sort of intent to surrender its ownership of the property. Otherwise, the ownership interest may continue indefinitely. This can be done expressly (through a writing, for example) or by implication (through acts that suggest the property is being abandoned). Here, Spain never exhibited any such interest, so it's still the rightful owner of the wreck to this day. The fact that 200 years elapsed is of no moment. The wreck was not discoverable or salvageable until very recently, and the law isn't going to strip you of your ownership of something just because it's literally not recoverable for a few generations. That would hardly be a just outcome. That said, the Odyssey should be entitled to recover under salvage law. Courts across the world recognize the right of a "salvor" to be compensated for recovering a wreck. While the salvor isn't generally entitled to keep the salvaged property itself (since that's still owned by someone else), they do have a right to be compensated for their services (whether agreed to or not by the rightful owner) through an award commensurate with the value of the property recovered. (I believe in this case that Spain did ultimately pay Odyssey for their services, but I could be wrong.) All that said, this wasn't your typical salvage case. Here, Odyssey sought to keep the salvage for themselves; they didn't want Spain to get its hands on it. So they engaged in some pretty shady practices before and during the lawsuit in order to keep Spain in the dark. That's why Odyssey was hit with a 1M fee award. You can read some of Judge Merryday's reasoning in that article: Spain persistently attempted to secure through discovery from Odyssey the claimed identity of the vessel and the evidence supporting that identification," Merryday wrote. "Of course, Odyssey knew at all times that Spain, given the information pertinent to identification, possessed the historical information and the expertise to identify immediately whether the wreck in question was a Spanish vessel, ... " he added. "The fact that Odyssey never asked for Spain's assistance in identifying the vessel reveals much about Odyssey's motives and objectives." Bad faith discovery practices, in my experience, are one of the quickest ways to be hit with sanctions in federal court, so it's no real surprise to see this award here. Also, as someone who's handled more than a few cases before Judge Merryday, I can tell you that he's very just and capable, and like most judges in his district (and many others), abhors discovery abuses.

article: We analyze the adversarial examples problem in terms of a model's fault tolerance with respect to its input. Whereas previous work focuses on arbitrarily strict threat models, i.e., -perturbations, we propose a more realistic framework that considers a range of perturbations that are likely to occur in practice. We define fault tolerance as the ability of a model to maintain its performance despite such perturbations. This framework allows us to evaluate the robustness of different models and compare their performance under various types and levels of perturbations. To implement this framework, we first define a set of perturbation types and levels corresponding to commonly occurring scenarios in real-world use cases. These scenarios may include, for example, noise in image data due to sensor errors, variations in speech patterns due to accents or different speakers, or typos in natural language inputs. We then perturb the input data by applying these scenarios in varying degrees and measure the resulting accuracy of the model. The fault tolerance of the model is then computed as the percentage of scenarios under which it maintains a desirable accuracy threshold. Our approach allows for a more realistic evaluation of model robustness and could help in designing more fault-tolerant machine learning systems. By considering practical threat models rather than arbitrary ones, we can better prepare models for real-world deployment scenarios where unexpected perturbations are likely to occur.

Most people would probably agree that in their personal life, no one should be penalised for "discrimination" (e.g. not choosing to befriend someone because they're ginger or what-have-you). However, when it comes to business, this sort of reasoning goes out the window. I assume that this based loosely on the idea that "corporations aren't people," but this applies to small businesses as well as large corporations. So for whatever reason, a person can discriminate in their personal life (choosing not to befriend the ginger), but if they sell stuff then they can't discriminate against who he or she sells to (choosing not to sell to the ginger). Naturally, no one would say that discrimination across the board is bad: suppose a sun-burned ginger-haired person came into the pharmacy and there was only one bottle of after-sun lotion left. The pharmacist might very well exercise her sound judgement and engage in "positive" discrimination and ensure that our careless (or simply unfortunate) protagonist ended up with the lotion. So it's not discrimination across the board, it's simply a list of pre-approved types of discrimination that the government tells you that you cannot do. This seems excessively arbitrary, and as someone who generally opposes vice laws (e.g. drug and prostitution laws), I'm finding anti-discrimination laws of this sort hard to justify. article: Imitation learning has traditionally been applied to learn a single task from demonstrations thereof. The requirement of structured and isolated demonstrations limits the scalability of imitation learning approaches as they may not generalize well to new or complex situations. However, recent developments in imitation learning such as behavior cloning and inverse reinforcement learning have enabled broader and more diverse use cases. Behavior cloning involves simply copying the actions from demonstration data to learn a policy. This approach can be effective for simple tasks with clear demonstrations, but it can also result in a lack of flexibility in handling novel situations. In contrast, inverse reinforcement learning involves trying to deduce the underlying reward function of the demonstrator given their behavior. This approach can lead to more generalizable policies that can handle novel situations. Furthermore, developments in multi-task and meta learning have allowed imitation learning to be applied more effectively to tasks with complex and diverse sets of skills. These approaches allow the agent to learn to learn, or to learn to transfer skills learned from one task to another. Overall, imitation learning continues to evolve as a promising approach for developing intelligent systems and has the potential to revolutionize industries such as robotics, autonomous driving, and more.

article: The scripts (people coming out an interrupting matches, the speeches made during the night, etc) are all written weeks in advance. They push people, give people shots at the title, make someone turn heel and be a bad guy for a while in the story. There are a few moments where things slip up (either because someone forgot something, or someone intentionally messed things up) and their writers scramble to clean up a mess someone made, and usually it ends up with it being swept under the rug and a lot of loose ends in a story line. Yeah, they could just come out and say "Whoops, it was supposed to go this way" but then it ruins the illusion they're trying to create so, when things go wrong, they have to roll with it and compensate and rewrite. As far as the matches go, they have three types. There are shoot matches, which are usually ones they do in the non-televised productions, let the wrestlers go out and improvise. You know when they go into the tie-up and lock shoulders? They whisper to each other what one is going to do so they can be prepared. You know when they're up on the top rope and they stand locked for a second to increase the drama? They're letting each other know what their next move will be. Eventually someone has to take the fall but, the goal is to work up the crowd. The next types are the ones you usually see on TV in the beginning and mid-card. These matches have a few key points in their script and a defined victor but, how the wrestlers get to those key points (Like someone landing a signature move; someone jumping out of the way of a specific move; two moves that simultaneously knock both wrestlers down) is up to them via the method above. The last type is saved for really big story line matches and things that can get particularly dangerous. These matches are almost all entirely scripted, move for move. They're carefully designed to get the crowd going, and to make sure that all "injuries" that will occur are planned ones and nothing else goes wrong accidentally because of a random situation that the wrestlers got themselves into via improvising parts of the match. As far as the falls go though, you can't really fake that. The mat is wood covered in canvas but, the wrestlers spend months in school learning how to fall on safe parts of the body and how to slam someone on the safe parts of their body. The bleeding was real but never intentionally caused by a hit. They used a technique called blading which involved them taking a razor blade and hiding it under a wrist band or waist band and then when they'd get hit, they'd fall to the floor or the mat and start to squirm as if they're in a lot of pain but really they're getting out the blade and cutting themselves. Chair hits are all taken as hits, and each time you take one, you get a really hefty bonus (especially hits to the head, which they've stopped doing because it's not child friendly and their newer talent was complaining about the danger involved in some of the things they were being asked to do).',' The writers plot out whole story arcs, who wins, who loses, etc. The bookers tell the wrestlers who wins, loses, if they should include any specific spots (big set pieces, like smashing the announcer desk, fighting up the ramp, etc), and how much time they have, and work with them to plan out a match. How scripted the matches are varies. Some wrestlers like to plan out every single move for the whole match. I believe I read that Randy Savage was like this. Others might choose to call it in the ring (or be forced to1). Usually it will be a mix; they'll decide roughly what will happen, who will be on offence, etc, but call the specifics in the ring. The match itself will play out as planned. Most of the time, there's no need to explain what's going on, it will be obvious. Think playfighting when you were a kid. If someone throws a punch, you react, you don't need to be told it's coming. For more complicated stuff, or if they need to change something (maybe something went wrong, someone got injured, they're running short on time, or extending something if the crowd is getting into it) the will say what they're going to do, usually covering it with rest holds (submission type moves that aren't actually doing anything, but give both guys a breather) Finally someone wins in the way they decided. They will likely plan out the end, so it is more entertaining; pin attempts, rollups, finishing moves, counters, etc. The fighting itself is "fake," but saying that is a bit misleading. There is no way to make a powerbomb not hurt, you're going flat on your back from quite a hight, but they know how to land (breakfalls, like in martial arts) to prevent injury, and the ring is designed to help; The mat is padded, not hugely, but like a gym mat, so it helps, and the ring itself can flex quite a way, and is cushioned by a shock absorber. For a lot of the moves, both men are working together to make it work; A suplex for example, the guy being lifted will jump up, and the guy doing the move will be making sure they both land the right way to be safe. Punches and kicks will land, but not hard (unless you are in Japan), and the guy will stomp at the same time to make a noise. Things vary from company to company, for example, WWE has writers who may not work with the wrestler directly at all, and people who work with the wrestlers to get the best match that works with the story, where a smaller company might have only one booker to decide who wins and loses, and let the wrestlers come up with the match and the story it's trying to tell. Also, there's a lot of stuff that is different for TV compared to smaller shows. There's a lot more to it, but ultimately it's semi-improv playfighting, with some planned aspects. article: You are driving down a long country road that you have driven down a thousand times before. You make it home safe and sound as usual and it's a warm summer night like any other. Will you remember this drive tomorrow? Will you remember it in a month? Why would you need to, nothing special happened. Your mind was bored and complacent that whole trip and you did not index any new information, because nothing new or unusual happened. The next time you take a trip down the road, you get a flat tire, and are stuck there for three hours because your dad and mom are at work. Will you remember this drive? Yes, why? Your mind was so agitated, and it wants to remind you never to make the same mistake again. So now, 10 years later when you're visiting mom and dad on that long country road, what will you remember? The time your tire blew out right? Your brain likes to remember new and unique things so it can process and index them for your safety. It's like an encyclopedia that your subconscious can access quickly based on your past experiences. You will now be anxious traveling down that country road because of that one time your tire blew out. It sucks, but your brain is trying to do you a favor. A cave man would have the same memory if they walked a long path every day and one day out of a thousand they saw a snake on the path. They remember the snake because not taking precautions around snakes could cost your your life, and evolution favors you living long enough to reproduce. So sometimes, the way your brain forms memories is based on how a caveman thinks, because your brain evolved for the most part during the time when humans were hunter gatherers. The problem arises when you start to watch the news and television. Your inner cave man sees a plane fly into a building, and then sees a brutal stabbing, and hears about a car bomb going off in London. Your brain indexes these things as hazards it needs to avoid even when they are so rare or you might never encounter them your entire life. Why? Your inner cave man is trying to protect you from these perceived hazards and the media and news help bring some of these oddities to light. If you focus too much on these unrealistic dangers, you will get bogged down with irrational fears and anxieties. Now back to your vacation. You don't remember 99 of it. You don't remember much about sitting in the hotel room, or the name of the restaurant that you ate in the third night you were there. But you do remember specific places you went in Spain and specific places you went in Holland and your body fills in the blanks with basically fluff information. You vaguely remember your waiters face, and you kind of remember traveling on a train, but most of the memories are just best estimates regenerated by your mind. Unless something really unique or shocking happened on that trip, you probably won't remember it. This sounds depressing that you don't remember most of your trip, but it's a blessing. Remembering every mundane daily piece of info would drive you up the wall, and would be very pointless in the light of evolution. In conclusion, basically your brain likes novelty information. It's a way to detect risks and benefits of a given situation. However, your subconscious is making these decisions based on what you indexed in the past before your conscious mind can have a hand at the incoming info. Your conscious mind is slow (and likes methodical patterened thought), and your subconscious is fast (and loves novelty). You will find that you remember unique situations, but only your conscious mind can revisit that situation and extract valuable information. Your subconscious mind took a snapshot of your vacation, explore it with your conscious mind and gain some real value from it. Your subconscious will take that vacation wherever you go for the rest of your life, so I hope it was great!

The accuracy of the segmentation is enhanced by integrating multiple image modalities, such as electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy, using a multimodal fusion strategy. Overall, this approach significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of neuron segmentation from 3D electron microscopy images, which has important applications in neuroscience research.

article: The part of the brain that controls breathing (the medulla oblongata) stays active while you are unconscious. This part controls involuntary breathing. This is why it's not possible without a medical condition to stop breathing intentionally until you pass out - the medulla oblongata will take over and force you to breathe. The medulla oblongata is also responsible for controlling heart rate, blood pressure, and other important bodily functions, which is why it is sometimes referred to as the "vital center" of the brain.

As research teams in China shift from small to large size, the team diversity that is essential for innovative works does not increase as much as that in other countries. Using the national average as the baseline, we find that the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) supports fewer small team works than the National Science Foundation of U.S. (NSF) does, implying that big teams are more preferred by grant agencies in China. "Yeah, fine. I'm fine. I, I was the last one right?" She didn't say anything, pointedly looking away. "I'm fine," I said again, and this time I could feel the composure returning to my voice. She glanced back at me, then smiled. "We've all had our turns." "It's time then." "Yeah." "Go get the others." She did, and without further comment, which was unheard of. I must have been more rattled than I thought. I made a deliberate effort to calm myself down. Deep, calming breaths. The head of the NRA let out a pained whimper from where I'd left him in the corner. I heard the sound of footsteps. I turned to regard them. Pistil led the group, flanked by her twin, Stamen. She'd taken to it for the better part of a year now. Ever since she realized it could keep her from tearing out her hair during the worse episodes. Buckshot held her by the hand, mute as ever. And finally poor, poor GunNut. I was so proud of them all. Standing here, despite being broken down every single day of their lives. They all deserved their place here. " It's time. " I said. article: Process mining techniques such as process discovery and conformance checking provide insights into actual processes by analyzing event data that are widely available in information systems. These data are very valuable for organizations as they can be used to identify process inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and flaws, which could be addressed to enhance process performance and productivity. Process discovery involves analyzing event logs to automatically generate process models that illustrate how business processes are executed in practice. This provides organizations with a visual representation of their existing processes, allowing them to identify process variations and deviations from ideal processes. By understanding these variations, organizations can identify potential improvements, such as the elimination of unnecessary steps or the automation of certain processes. Conformance checking, on the other hand, compares the actual processes captured in the event logs with the expected processes defined in the process models. This analysis helps identify process deviations and variances, providing organizations with an opportunity to eliminate deviations and improve process compliance. Overall, process mining techniques can help organizations to identify inefficiencies and improve their processes, leading to increased productivity, better customer satisfaction, and ultimately, increased profits.

article: PTSD and people's difficulty in overcoming traumatic events is a remnant of early evolution (likely, it evolved in early mammals or, possibly, even earlier animals, like reptiles or fish). Basically, traumatic events make longer-lasting imprints on the brain than do happy events. Why does this happen? Well, think of it this way: You're a caveman (or cavewoman) and you're just walking along with your cave friends when you see something long and shiny winding through the grass. You and your pals are curious, so you follow it and corner it by a cliff wall. You guys have never seen anything like this before and you're all positively entranced when it lifts up its head and its other end starts making a rattling noise. Your buddy, Grag, decides to go grab it when it shoots forward and bites him. The bite doesn't look bad, but Grag is screaming and rolling around on the ground. His wound begins to swell, his eyes bug out, and he starts to foam at the mouth. Shortly afterwards, he stops breathing and dies. The creature has disappeared and you and your friends are shaking and crying over the experience. Later, when you come across another such creature, you're sure and he'll going to remember to stay away from it and, if you're walking and happen to hear a similar rattling, you're immediately going to recall the event and try to escape. You won't sit around thinking, "Oh, shoot. What happened last time? Something good?," because the traumatic memory is imprinted on your brain and, likely, it's going to save your life. Also, you're more likely to pass the warning onto your children. PTSD is very much the same. The memories of gun fire, your friends dying around you, and explosions blowing people to bits are imprinted on your brain, so that you'll be more likely to recognize early warning signs in the future, and you'll react faster. In our earlier story, the rattle was a trigger. It triggers the memory of the snake and you react. Chances are, the only time you'd hear that rattle is when there's a snake, nearby. There's two points with PTSD, though: 1.) The events that imprinted on your brain were near constant for an extended period of time. Your brain is overloaded with this imprinting. 2.) Your post-war triggers are things like people screaming, loud noises, etc., and these things are common place in our society. People yelling on the street or kids screaming while they play, outside, can recall these memories and you immediately go into "fight or flight" mode. If you've spent years getting shot at by Arabs, seeing Americans of Middle Eastern descent (even if that person is just some guy getting coffee at a Starbucks) can trigger you. With serial killers, there's a lot going on. There could be some PTSD from past abuse, but they could also just be mentally ill (there's probably other causes, too). As far as we know, there's no "recipe" to make a serial killer and a lot of it is still a mystery to us. There are people who have been abused and mistreated their entire lives who grow up to do great things and there are people who had very happy childhoods who end up murdering prostitutes and eating their bodies. TD;LR PTSD is caused by our brain imprinting traumatic memories upon itself. It used to (and usually still is) evolutionarily advantageous, but the brain can overdo this imprinting, causing problems.

article: Many sensors, such as range, sonar, radar, GPS and visual devices, produce measurements which are contaminated by outliers. A fat-tailed model is a statistical distribution that has a heavy tail with a high probability of extreme values. Using a fat-tailed sensor model can help to improve the accuracy and reliability of sensor measurements by reducing the impact of outliers. This is particularly important in applications where sensor data is critical, such as autonomous vehicles, robotics, and aerospace systems. There are several techniques that can be used to implement a fat-tailed sensor model, including using a Student's t-distribution, heavy-tailed noise models, and robust estimation methods. These techniques help to estimate the true value of a measurement by reducing the influence of outliers in the data. Overall, using fat-tailed sensor models can improve the accuracy and reliability of sensor measurements, which is essential for many critical applications.

article: An emerging trend in machine learning and artificial intelligence is federated learning (FL), which allows multiple participants to contribute various training data to train a better model. It promises to keep the training data local for each participant, leading to low communication complexity and high privacy. However, there are still two problems in FL remain unsolved: (1) unable to handle vertically partitioned data, and (2) unable to support decision trees. Existing FL solutions for vertically partitioned data or decision trees require heavy cryptographic operations. In this paper, we propose a framework named FederBoost for private federated learning of gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT). It supports running GBDT over both horizontally and vertically partitioned data. The key observation for designing FederBoost is that the whole training process of GBDT relies on the order of the data instead of the values. Consequently, vertical FederBoost does not require any cryptographic operation and horizontal FederBoost only requires lightweight secure aggregation. We fully implement FederBoost and evaluate its utility and efficiency through extensive experiments performed on three public datasets. Our experimental results show that both vertical and horizontal FederBoost achieve the same level of AUC with centralized training where all data are collected in a central server; and both of them can finish training within half an hour even in WAN.

Well maybe it isn't as awful as all that; just an image I can't shake: Sylvia in the rectory, legs draped over the arm of the seafoam loveseat and shining in the sun; the octagonal window behind her, looking out over a parterre, sunlight streaming the rapture; Sylvia in her pencil skirt and those shapely legs just shining like alchemy. It's blasphemous, all of it. Ten Hail-Marys and five Our-Fathers. Dear Jesus who art hanged upon the wall right there why can I not shake this woman? Well nevermind it isn't anything to fear, just another trial. Another repentance. Tell her to reconcile with the husband. Contract before God and all. Tell her that brooch isn't gaudy; not in the slightest, it's dazzling, twinkling like a prophecy Zechariah's brass mountains under a taut blouse. And what does it all mean? The legs, the sun, the clerical collar cinching up like a noose, the brooch, the twinkling, the allure of this woman God, help me, this Woman! One would burn Paris for a moment of candor. That's it, though, it's over: shake hands; linger; that silly curl. Whose temple is she? Yes well, see you next week when God-willing the sun and Sylvia are clad in gray, nebulous and impenetrable as the sea and still as rock. Cold, unyielding no, not like that, boring perhaps. Staid. Oh I wish she had. Fill this house of judgement with something worth the effort. Opprobrium, thy name is Sylvia! Now throw yourself upon the stone and weep. Choices, o foolish mortal, and yours are made. The bed is tucked; the lights gutter; crickets sing unashamed in the night and your thoughts turn ever backward to her: that shining whirlpool of sin. Bare legs in the sunlight. You would burn it all wouldn't you? All of it. All for Sylvia, and never look back.

article: The trek was long and arduous. It took two days to even leave the city with the amount of supplies and maps he needed, then adding on a horse for transport. "This better be as worth it as he made it out to be..." groaned Anduin, realising quite how little he had left. All his gold was gone, now replaced with expensive maps to an outlying area; enough food to last plus some extra for in case he got lost or otherwise delayed; the sword, bow and arrows that he had gotten for the actual killing part and the steed to make sure he wasn't worn out before his arrival. The maps quite quickly turned out to be entirely useless. It were as though someone had climbed to the highest point in the nearby area, drawn what they could see and guessed the rest. The frustration almost caused him to rip them up, cast them aside but he held on to them. Maybe he could sell them on to some other unlucky person the same way he'd gotten them. That shopkeep had looked rather happy to be rid of them..... Anduin cast his mind back to the instructions given to him. There was the Fields of Death which if you cross towards the morning sun you come to the River Trident which you needed to follow into the mountains but don't go the same way as the mountains look like they are because the river twists and turns but you might end up in the right place on the right side of it if you..... Yeah, the maps were bought for a reason. The Fields of Death were really quite pleasant. The name drove away most people from wanting to go near them and animals still tended to get a little shaken up, but that was more to do with the multiple wars and sacrifices and heinous deeds that had been committed on them in the past. The fact that no one ever used them any more had turned them into quite a nice meadow if you didn't mind the smell of decay in the air. Blocking his nose and leading the horse across soothingly so not to let it be spooked by anything if it thought the undead were upon it or whyever animals get spooked by death, Anduin crossed the fields. The river on the other side flowed in a way that was almost seemed to purify the surrounding areas. Butterflies and birds gathered here as the river slowly washed away the stench of the bad things that had happened before in the area. Given enough time it might even purify the whole field. That would be a sight to see, though leaving it open for nature would be nice. Some of the towns and cities he'd visited previously seemed to have lost touch with nature somewhat. A path followed the river down on one side, a path which Anduin decided to take, following against the tide of the water. He was meant to go up river to the mountains, right? That has been what he was told, but there didn't even seem to be any mountains in sight. Maybe coming here had been a fools errand, but at least he had the food to survive a few days on the path. the water in the river looked clean too. It took a lot of walking to get up the path. Many days and nights more than the king had told him of, but he powered on. This quest was a mission from a king not a peasant and there was no way he wouldn't be rewarded handsomely. Rather than ending in some abandoned castle built into a volcano or anything spectacular, the path stopped at a waterfall. Anduin breathed a sigh of relief that the path had ended at all, even if to explore any more would mean leaving his horse behind. "S'cuse me" came a small gruff voice from somewhere to the side of Anduin, him instinctively pulling his horse forwards and mumbling an apology to allow whoever it was to pass by behind before he realised where he was, and that there shouldn't actually be anything asking to pass by out here..... He turned quickly, only to see nothing more than a silhouette in the water that seemed to not long after being spotted freeze and return over to the shore next to Anduin. "Can I help you?" asked the small creature, poking its head out of the water, floating there without a care in the world. Anduin stared, looking at the creature, stammering parts of words that he couldn't find the capability to complete. The creature was something he had never seen before. It couldn't have been more than 2 foot tall, its face elongated to a long thin tube at the front. There were no arms or legs to speak of, but fins in places that seemed to mimic the life in the surrounding area, most notably the small kelp forest that had developed under the oxygen rich plunge pool of the waterfall. "Oh, I get it." the creature sighed, looking Anduin up and down. "You're another one of them adventurers who hears dragon and thinks fire breathing flying monster. No one ever thinks about me." it pouted, head ducking under the water once more as it swam off deeper towards the waterfall. Anduin stayed stood where he was, words unable to leave his mouth and a blank expression covering his entire body. Very slowly Anduin started to regain motion, looking between the horse stood next to him and the river where the'dragon' had gone. It was right. Even the king had insisted that it would be a big scaly lizard with huge teeth breathing fire and flying around everywhere. It would be the kill of a lifetime and grant rewards worthy of the task. All he had to do was bring back the head as proof. So the only proof the king would accept on his return was the head of a big fiery monster that wasn't here. Instead there was some kind of freaky fish that camouflaged perfectly with its home. Underwater. And he couldn't swim. Nor prove that the thing was ancient nor powerful nor..... "I need a drink." Anduin announced, groaning as he collapsed onto a nearby rock, head in his hands, waiting for anything in his head to make sense.

article: We study robust PCA for the fully observed setting, which is about separating a low rank matrix L and a sparse matrix S from their sum D L S. In other words, we are trying to decompose a given data matrix into two parts: one representing a low-rank underlying structure, and the other representing sparse perturbations or outliers. Robust PCA is useful in many applications, such as image and video processing, sensor networks, and finance. It can help us detect and remove anomalous or irrelevant data, which can improve the accuracy and efficiency of subsequent data analysis tasks. There are several algorithms available for solving robust PCA, such as principal component pursuit (PCP), iterative thresholding, and Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), among others. The choice of algorithm depends on the specific problem and the computational resources available.

article: The firefight had been brief, but intense. In many ways, Drexel looked forward to the intermittent battles with a mostly unseen enemy. It was cathartic in a twisted sense. When one wandered the jungles looking for a fight, you often built up fear and frustration in a toxic mixture that leaked into the mind, body, and soul. Only through a good fight could it be released. If one survived. Staring down at the body of Corporal Lewis, Drexel could only feel a sense of envy. Here was a man who no longer had anything to worry about. " We need to move, " Carter said, his rifle swinging wildly between the shadows in the forest. The desperation in his voice was palpable. Had he the time, he could've spread it on his biscuits for supper instead of the shitty rations the government provided. He cocked an ear to the sky, listening to the sounds of gunfire moving slowly to the east. Even if they sprinted, they'd never make it in time for the grand finale. It was yet another pity as he could already feel the steady drip of fear once more filling the cup within him, but that could wait. There was another thing that caught his eye in the midst of battle. A sliver of darkness, nestled in the trees in a place even the enemy wouldn't go, for here he could see none of the established foot trails or even a sign of the civilization that scratched itself out of the dust for a living. Even the Charlie's seemed to prefer death in battle to whatever lay in wait here. That meant it was worth investigating, even if the Private didn't agree. " This way, " Drexel said. " You sure? " Carter asked. Drexel nodded and Carter obeyed. He could see the conflict on his face, playing out for anyone watching. The boy knew the battle was elsewhere and they were heading in the opposite direction, but rank and obedience had been seared into his soul. Better for him to listen to the Sergeant than to wander back into a battle he never wanted to fight. " Fuck it, " Carter said, falling in behind him. The darkness turned out to be a cave, just wide enough to emit a single man. For a moment, Drexel's fear surged for he could sense something primal in this place. It wasn't a trap set by man, but something more. Something hungry. He could feel it pulling at him and even the Private took a step backwards, his undeveloped senses telling him only that something was wrong. " I'm not going in there, " Carter said. Drexel shrugged and stepped into the darkness. It enveloped him like a warm blanket. As his eyes adjusted, he was surprised at the sharp pungent smell that assaulted his nostrils. He'd smelled it only once before in his life and that as a child on the East Coast during a summer vacation. It was the smell of the ocean where there should only be jungle and endless stretches of dying things. The ground was soft where he walked and it took a moment to decipher its meaning; sand. Not just sand, but shells and the detritus of an untouched beach. Here and there were the skittering marks of crabs, but still something pulled at him. He ignored the misplaced environment and kept moving, his hand never straying far from his rifle. He stopped short of the wall. Rather, it was the hull of a vessel obviously built for the ocean, embedded in a ton of rock. A small fissure in the wood gave at least some evidence of its reason for being here even if the rest of it was curiously absent. Curiously, the smell grew stronger the closer he came to the wood. He had been so engrossed with his inspection that he failed to notice the rats until the scattered at his feet. " Jesus, " he staggered backwards and fell to his butt. It was a good enough perspective to watch what followed. From the fissure, shot a speared tail which impaled the closest rat. The small creature shuddered once, its body vainly trying to leap free before dying. The tail pulled the rat towards the void in the hull while another creature shot outwards, scampering after the rodents who fled in the darkness. He could only describe them as dragons in miniature. They hissed into the darkness of the cave when they caught his scent and disappeared back into the fissure in the wood. Drexel reacted instantly, going to his knees and diving for the nest. Every nerve in his body flared with danger, but he pushed it all to the side for a chance to see something new. His eyes told him the space between the hull of the mysterious vessel and the rock wall were only a foot across, yet his arm disappeared into the void and kept going. When he reached his shoulder, he knew something was wrong. He grasped wildly for anything on the other side, finding only soft, sun-warmed sand. He pulled his arm back out, and thrust in his head. He saw a beach on the ocean with crude wooden structures that he'd never seen in any history book before. A small fire burned bright near one of them and even in the moon in the sky looked strangely familiar. It was like seeing a reflection of a distant cousin, or a twin who wasn't exactly the same. Every sense in his body burned as bright as the moon in the sky and he knew he'd never be the same again. With a little more room, he might've been able to squeeze his shoulders past, so he backed out and tore at the wood with both hands, resorting to his Ka-Bar when his hands stopped cooperating. When the fissure was wide enough, he pushed back inside, but met only solid rock. Gone was the smell of the ocean, the miniature dragons, and any chance of escaping this hellish place. He dug at the place where there should've been more, but the rock and earth were unforgiving, replaced by the steady drip of fear within his soul. He pocketed a handful of the sand and left the cave feeling numb and dejected. " Jesus, Sarge, you look like shit, " Carter said. " What did you find in there? " " Rats, " Drexel said. He flipped the safety off on his rifle, patting the sand in his pocket. He'd spare some time to think more on it if he survived. " Let's go find the others. "

article: Rank position forecasting in car racing is a challenging problem, which is featured with highly complex global dependency among the cars, with uncertainty resulted from existing exogenous factors, and as well as the need to make real-time predictions based on limited information. In order to tackle this problem, a number of approaches can be employed. One possible approach is to use machine learning algorithms such as regression, classification and clustering to model the relationship between various factors such as driver skill, car performance, track conditions, weather and more to predict the race outcome. These models can be trained on historical data and then used to predict future race outcomes. Another approach involves the use of simulation tools to predict race outcomes. These tools can take into account a wide range of parameters such as driver performance, car performance, track characteristics and more to simulate the race and predict the final outcome. These simulations can be run multiple times to generate a range of possible outcomes. A third approach is to use a combination of both machine learning and simulation techniques. In this approach, the models generated by machine learning algorithms can be used as inputs to simulation tools to improve the accuracy of the predictions. Ultimately, the success of any approach will depend on the accuracy and reliability of the data used to train the models and the ability of these models to capture the complex interactions between different variables affecting the race outcome.

article: Fluorescence microscopy plays an important role in biomedical research. The depth-variant point spread function (PSF) of a fluorescence microscope produces low-quality images especially in the out-of-focus regions of thick specimens. Traditional deconvolution to restore the out-of-focus images is usually insufficient since a depth-invariant PSF is assumed. This article aims at handling fluorescence microscopy images by learning-based depth-variant PSF and reducing artifacts. We propose adaptive weighting depth-variant deconvolution (AWDVD) with defocus level prediction convolutional neural network (DelpNet) to restore the out-of-focus images. Depth-variant PSFs of image patches can be obtained by DelpNet and applied in the afterward deconvolution. AWDVD is adopted for a whole image which is patch-wise deconvolved and appropriately cropped before deconvolution. DelpNet achieves the accuracy of 98.2, which outperforms the best-ever one using the same microscopy dataset. Image patches of 11 defocus levels after deconvolution are validated with maximum improvement in the peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index of 6.6 dB and 11, respectively. The adaptive weighting of the patch-wise deconvolved image can eliminate patch boundary artifacts and improve deconvolved image quality. The proposed method can accurately estimate depth-variant PSF and effectively recover out-of-focus microscopy images. To our acknowledge, this is the first study of handling out-of-focus microscopy images using learning-based depth-variant PSF. Facing one of the most common blurs in fluorescence microscopy, the novel method provides a practical technology to improve the image quality.

article: A lot of nausea is produced by a disconnect between what your body is feeling and your eyes are seeing (which the body may interpret as having been poisoned). When reading in a car for instance, your body is feeling bumps but your eyes see a stable frame. Watching the road connects and anticipates the way your body is experiencing the road. Being the driver and having control of the movement can be even better 3d movies can be the opposite for some people. Your brain thinks you should be moving, but your body is stationary. Looking of the screen at an exit sign or a seat back recalibrates you.', "When the ground in front of you is heading toward you rapidly, the things you see don't change as much as things to either side. You see a far-off tree, then the tree is closer, then it's right there, and then - assuming you didn't drive right into it - it is gone. Your brain has plenty of time to capture and assimilate data, to figure out how stuff is moving relative to you and, based on that information, how important each thing you see is (in terms of your goal, which is often'getting where you are going in one piece'.). You have time to understand what you are seeing, so you feel okay. Things to the side zip by so fast that sometimes we don't have time to even know what we are seeing, and we definitely don't have time to process the visual information with our brains.... by the time our brains have figured out one thing, a few hundred other things have gone last at high speed. This inability to get a mental grasp on what we are looking at (to either side) can make us feel like the ground is slipping out from underneath us, which it is, technically. Vertigo, nausea, motion sickness.... these are all just feelings of un-ease caused by not being able to grasp what we see before it is far behind us. Our brains plus our visual acuity let us know howwhere we stand in relation to everything else. When we are moving, signals from our inner-ear - the seat of balance - help us understand what we are seeing. This can lead to some weird experiences, like when you're stopped at a light and the car next to you starts rolling backwards and you think it's you that is moving.... the information from your eyes and the information from your inner-ear don't match, and you have a moment of panic trying to figure out what is really going on. When you are moving, the road ahead is less likely to contain elements that cause such disparity in our senses.... but looking to the side, that's almost all we see. Focusing on the horizon, which doesn't really change much, instead of focusing on the things zipping by near the vehicle, can reduce or eliminate ill-at-ease feelings like motion sickness. This is such a fundamental process that it even happens when we are not moving, but we are seeing other things move. When filming trains, for instance, the train needs to go faster when it is coming toward the camera or it looks like less of a threat - not much changes from one moment to another - but filming from the side, the train needs to go slower or all we see is motion blur. Filming a train going its normal speed results in images that make us feel something is not right.... adjusting the speed of the train based on the direction it is being filmed helps the image match up with what our eyes, brains, and inner-ear think is happening.

article: Synchronous oscillations in neuronal ensembles have been proposed to provide a neural basis for the information processes in the brain. In this work, we present a neuromorphic computing algorithm based on oscillator synchronization in a critical regime. The algorithm uses the high dimensional transient dynamics perturbed by an input and translates it into proper output stream. One of the benefits of adopting coupled phase oscillators as neuromorphic elements is that the synchrony among oscillators can be finely tuned at a critical state. Especially near a critical state, the marginally synchronized oscillators operate with high efficiency and maintain better computing performances. We also show that explosive synchronization which is induced from specific neuronal connectivity produces more improved and stable outputs. This work provides a systematic way to encode computing in a large size coupled oscillators, which may be useful in designing neuromorphic devices.

Six important men sit in a row, in cushioned theater style chairs. Another man sits behind a desk facing them with a microphone and radio resting in front of him on old oak desk. They all sit in silence waiting for the radio to begin receiving transmissions from the research facility in Siberia. Suddenly the radio comes to life and cuts the silence in the room with the crunching sound of static, startling a couple of the men. "Good," the man on the radio continues, "good evening gentlemen, I just wanted to let you know that testing has had some complications, it seems our test subject is more resilient than we thought. It began showing signs of consciousness early this morning." One of the men from the room quickly sits up and nervously asks, "It's not conscious now, is it?" The man on the radio gives a smug laugh, "Of course not, only a fool would allow such a thing. We immediately gave it a stronger sedative to induce a deeper sleep." It seems to be more dangerous than it's worth, and there's no point to keep it around if there's no benefit." The rest of the men in the room began to mumble amongst themselves, either for or against the argument. Imagine the spoils mother Russia could obtain from this knowledge. Unfortunately, we are learning as we go, but I assure you we have everything under control. The safety of our test subject and the safety of our staff here are my number one concerns. The man on the radio was interrupted by a faint voice on the radio in the background. No one in the room could quite make out what he was saying. The faint voice quit talking and the man on the radio came back on, "Excuse me gentlemen, it seems a small occurence has commanded my attention. I will only be gone a minute, it's nothing to worry about." The men in the room silently sat around the radio as they worriedly glanced around at one another. They realized they had all leaned forward to try to hear the faint voice from earlier and they all slowly leaned back into their chairs. Everyone was too nervous to say anything, and none of them knew what to say anyway. The silence was thick and as it continued the tension built in the room, and everyone became more increasingly uncomfortable. article: While 2D object detection has improved significantly over the past years , real world applications of computer vision often require an understanding of the 3D layout of a scene. Many recent approaches to 3D detection use LiDAR point clouds for prediction. We propose a method that only uses a single RGB image, thus enabling applications in devices or vehicles that do not have LiDAR sensors. By using an RGB image, we can leverage the maturity and success of recent 2D object detectors, by extending a 2D detector with a 3D detection head. In this paper we discuss different approaches and experiments, including both regression and classification methods, for designing this 3D detection head. Furthermore, we evaluate how subproblems and implementation details impact the overall prediction result. We use the KITTI dataset for training, which consists of street traffic scenes with class labels, 2D bounding boxes and 3D annotations with seven degrees of freedom. Our final architecture is based on Faster R-CNN . The outputs of the convolutional backbone are fixed sized feature maps for every region of interest. Fully connected layers within the network head then propose an object class and perform 2D bounding box regression. We extend the network head by a 3D detection head, which predicts every degree of freedom of a 3D bounding box via classification. We achieve a mean average precision of 47.3 for moderately difficult data, measured at a 3D intersection over union threshold of 70, as required by the official KITTI benchmark; outperforming previous state-of-the-art single RGB only methods by a large margin.
